title: Our national recreation parks [1], 1903
transcription:
Preface
This little book conveys the impressions made upon and during a visit to our Great National Recreation Parks - The Yellowstone and Yosemite Valley during my recent summer vacation. An inspection of these wonderlands cannot fail in leaving lasting impressions of their manifold indescribable beauties, exquisite illustrations of national art and exhaustless resources of nature's ceaseless activities. The many enchanting sceneries defy description and accounts of the hundreds of mysterious geysers and the Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone and the big trees of the Sierras

title: Our national recreation parks [1], 1903
transcription: sound like fairy tales. No visitor who has ever seen these natural parks has ever been disappointed in his expectations. The alpine and subalpine regions with their great primeval forests, bewitching lakes, the numerous mountain springs and rivers teeming with choicest fish, the charming flora and varied fauna furnish object lessons from the book of nature which attract the eye and engage the mind from sunrise to sunset and the cool nights and pure mountain air will bring back sleep if it has been chased away by an

title: Our national recreation parks [1], 1903
transcription:
exacting arduous artificial city life. No where in the world can a vacation of a few weeks be spent more pleasantly and profitably than by a visit to these parks which have been set aside by a generous and farsighted Government as Recreation Grounds for the benefit of the people. To those who would like to see the most beautiful sceneries and nature's grandest products and exhibitions of art I would unhesitatingly say: "Come and see."
Chicago, Christmas 1903

title: Our national recreation parks [1], 1903
transcription:
Our National Recreation Parks
N Senn 1903
The man who toils with his brain in the bank, the pulpit, the courtroom the library the great mercantile establishments, and last but not least at the bedside of the sick or in the operating room is the one above all others in need of an occasional rest, change of mental activity and surroundings. Men who ignore nature's warnings and appeals for rest, sooner or later are made to pay dearly for their neglect and only too often mend their ways when it is too late. Brain toil means the prolonged strenuous application of the neurons which preside over functions

title: Our national recreation parks [1], 1903
transcription:
2
required in the discharge of professional duties, or business transactions. If these functions are overtaxed brain fatigue is the result. This brain fatigue involves that part of the brain which has been overtaxed while the remaining neurons are suffering from the consequences of idleness. Indigestion, insomnia and a morose temper are the earliest and surest indications of brain exhaustion and when they do appear must be heeded by the sufferer who then should seek the necessary relief by appropriate rest and change of surroundings. Loss of sleep is responsible for much of the unhappiness in this world and innumerable acts of desperation. Sleep is the brain's staunchest ally and when it hides itself

title: Our national recreation parks [1], 1903
transcription:
3
the delicate machinery will soon rebel against the most indomitable will. Insomnia is the brain toiler's worst enemy.
O sleep, O gentle sleep, 
Nature's soft nurse! how have I frightened thee,
That thou no more wilt weigh my eyelids down
And steep my senses in forgetfulness?
(Shakespeare)
If the sufferer from insomnia begins battle with his enemy by substituting artificially induced sleep for natural sleep his downfall will be speedy and certain. The average physician when consulted by the sleepless sufferers give the well meant advise to cease work and seek rest. This advise even when promptly accepted and carried into effect is often void of the expected results for

title: Our national recreation parks [1], 1903
transcription:
4
Powerful indeed is the empire of habit
(Publius Syrus).
What is rest for some is toil to others. Idleness is not rest. The needed rest is rest for the over-burdened neurons and useful employment for the neurons which have been at a standstill. The fashionable summer resorts, crowded, noisy cities [[forced?]] journeys and luxurious clubs are not congenial to the sufferer from brain fatigue. "Indolence that dangerous siren, must be eschewed, or thou must be content to yield up whatever thou hast acquired by the nobler exertions of thy life." (Horatius)
Labor is man's mission on earth and when the monotony of one kind of strenuous exertion creates fatigue a change of work and surroundings brings the much desired repose.

title: Our national recreation parks [1], 1903
transcription:
The artisan and farmer when affected by muscle fatigue will find the busy city interesting, instructive and restful, the brain toiler should seek rest and relief in nature's work shops and art galleries where there are no telephones, no telegraphs, no daily news and where the screech of the steam whistle and the hum of manufactories have no access. The trees, the shrubs, the flowers and the birds are the best friends of the weary fretful soul.
The most successful physician is he who finds and removes the cause of disease. In no other disease is this more important than in brain tire. The most frequent cause of brain fatigue is care, a fact recognized by

title: Our national recreation parks [1], 1903
transcription:
the poet of all poets when he said:
I am sure care's an enemy to life (Shakespeare).
For the intelligent mind, there is no loneliness in the solitude. Nature's handiwork is everywhere. It is seen in the desert, in the prairies in the forests, the rivers, the lakes and the countless forms of animal and vegetable life.
Man is never alone. During the day busy nature is the entertainer and at night the every varying sky is the silent instructor.
The seeker for mental repose away from all care in the midst of solitude will become conscious of the fact that
"He is never less at leisure than when at leisure" (Cicero)

Letters to John and Annie
Prayer meeting Mr. Cadmers. Nette, Ely & Flroence sent to hear the Bell Ringers thereafter. No teachers' Meeting.

Fri.19      Teaching 2 days       6.00
                 Washing                    1.10
Called at W. J. Gardner's and at Maud Fowl's. The letter with Miss Luella Phipps -- tried to call on Miss Pauline Johnson but did not find her in. Geo. Rich came in, in evening.

Sat         Bread, 5 loaves     39      
                Cookies                    25
Dinner Fried pork, Rice Croquettes, Salsify. Indian Pudding. 
Letter for Being Brave. Harry sang at funeral of Mrs. Andrew Fowl. Nette went to see Bessie Haines. 
Made 3 loaves brown bread.

Sun. 21   Cloudy all day. Rain & Snow.
Mr. Cadmers preached on Joshua 5:12. Old  [[?]] & manna. All to c. & S.S.  6 in my class. Dunham Rich, Chushill, Braman.

Day,. Park. Letters to Wilder, J Harl, Harold Mays, address sent to Chas. Pomrry  [[?]]
Dinner Baked Beans, cold meat, appliie pie & cream. Ch & S.S.  teach           10

title: Marion Metcalf diary [10], 1892-1901
transcription:
Monday- February. 22 
Bread          16
Fortnightly Meet at Mrs Haine' entertained by Bessie and Nette. I made peanut cakes there-for. Florence and I went also + I enjoyed it very much. Home a little after 5. Latin in evening. Letter from Mr Turner_ also one from Carrie, telling of their housekeeping plans_
Tues. 23- Made biscuit for breakfast, + took 6:30 car for Cleveland to see the Hampton People. 
Cleveland + ret.                           85
car fare. to Univ. Sch. + back   10
Car fare, extra- dumm.             05
Bread                                              16
Mrs. French, milk_                            50
No lesson with Fay-
Wed. 24 Mrs Wallace milk-             25
Florence + I went to Obelin at 11:27 train 15 minutes late. I found A+A Mayo + Franse at dinner- Went to see Miss Little and to Mrs Andrews to hunt up things for Carrie_ also had hair cut. Back at 5:07, stopped at chapel for supper, Pater came also. 150 or more there to supper, including mr Cadmis. Folded clothes in evening- letters to John + Carrie, Emily Wheeler, + Miss Josephine Walker. 
Southern Workman-              100
Plantation Songs                      50

title: Marion Metcalf diary [10], 1892-1901
transcription:
Oberline + ret-                     30
Hair Cut                                 15
Bread                                     08
Thurs. Bread                        21
Callers all the afternoon. Mrs Leonard + Mrs Barnhart. Miss Herff + Miss Randall who want to give an entertainment in her church. Miss Hulbert here. Prayer meeting + Teacher's Meeting. Mr Calmus at both.
Fri. Cold, snowy. Harry had his paper on Early Life of Lincoln in Club this evening. Tried to make custard pie with soda biscuit for crust. Oatmeal griddle cakes for breakfast- bought loaf of rye bread yesterday-
Miss Hulbert                      100
Mrs Fay. Latin. .25 too much pd to Mar 1.       5.00
  "              milk                                                          1 00
Sat. Miss Hall. milk                                               1 00
Mrs Nichols       "                                                       05
Bread                                  27
Washing                           1 10
Lizzie + Mrs Frank DeWitt came up in PM. Baked Apples, made Snow Pudding + Poor Man's Bread- Called at Benton's, Ely's, Mussey, Bowen.
Sunday. Feb. 28 Some snowstorms, starlight evening. Went to church in evening with Minnie. 2 good sermons today- only 3 in my S.S. class- Geo Rich, Mr Dunham Harry Braman- Beans. Cold Meat_ Snow Pud

title: Marion Metcalf diary [10], 1892-1901
transcription:
John came back, late to dinner -
Ivette drove Florence Putnam over to Merlin. I did not  return. Pate[[?]] + b[[?]] picked grapes.
Dinner - Bean Soup. Hash. Fried Apples. Blanc Mange.
Heard from Mrs. Kelsey. letter fr. Sister Moore, e[[/]elring one fr. Dora Freman. Keyes had a letter from Donald McFarland, in Des Moines.
Tues. 13. Papering finished in easter room upstairs . Went as Reception room. to meet train at 4:08, 4:18, 5:07, 5:30, 6:50, 7:50, 7:57, 8:03. Mrs. Kelsey came at 5:07. + Ely took her home. In the evening we brought home Miss Rispa[[l]] Jarrod, [[?]] Mr. Vernon.
Eng. Monkey for supper.
Wed. 14 Went to meet train at 11:27 + 11:55 + 2:07. Dinner at M. Eilah- Annual Meeting of Ohio Branch of W.B. M [[?]] in our church today + tomorrow. Mrs. Wood living of Boston soike finely in evening on work of A.M.A. Children Meeting at H. I took keyes and Nelemand to same. Miss Hobart, F Cleveland, came to our home after the afternoon meeting
Miss Jam hairing gone to Pearl Lord's.
Thurs 15 F.M. day- Went down about 11 + staid till nearly 6 - went with Mrs. Kelsey to 5:30 train. Dinner at M.E.Ch. John + Carrie drove over to Oberlin in P.M.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [10], 1892-1901
transcription:
Lovely weather. 
Prayer meeting in evening. Very tired-
Friday 16. Six quarts Grape preserves. Grape juice made for Jelly. Called on Mrs DeLong. did a little mending. Chipped Beef in milk. Fried potato. String Beans. Grapes. Poor Man's Pudding. Cool & cloudy.
Sat. 17. Great McKinley Parade + Mass Meeting. Bicycles. Bands. Cavalry. Speeches by Business + Burrows. 21 glasses Grape Jelly. Catawba. 4 loaves Eggless Cake (buttermilk) 4 apple pies _ 2 tins biscuit. Much bread.
English Monkey for dinner_ Pear Sauce. Sent apples to Mrs DeLong. Jack went to Madison to preach.
Cool, cloudy. some rain-
Sunday 18. Cloudy. snow in the air most of the day. All went to church except Carrie and Franklin. I went in evening also. Text in A.M. "The foundation of God standeth sure"- Hard frost this morning- fine, clear day till towards night- Minnie came back about 7:30P.M. so no washing today, alas! Teacher's Meeting small, but good. Harry went to Personal Work class. Wrote letter to Mrs Murphy, of Mt. Vernon, Mr. Mc Farland's cousin.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [10], 1892-1901
transcription:
Hat.   2.25
3 whiskbrooms @ 13   39
Plaid cloth- 3 yds. 1.50 [[? dig Leuch's]]-
Dr + Mrs DeLong left town. John asked to preach for next two Sunday. Franklin + I went down town in AM.   Tuesday. Oct. 20.
Wed. 21. Pater + John went to Confession in Berea. Pater was there over night last night. Pater + I went to chapel to supper. Miss Monroe, Mrs. Harris & others, entertained. had some talk with Mr + Mrs Chas Savage.
Thurs. 22. Jack led the prayer meeting on Daily Uses of the Bible. Very good too.
Fri.23. Miss Wadsworth here yesterday + today, making over my old blue dress.
Sat. 24. Trying to get ready to go to DesMoines. Ely bought my ticket this evening. Began to pack trunks +c.
Sunday 25. Pater had one of his bad turns this afternoon, came out of it rather quicker than usual. Harry +I went to the jail. Mr Webster did the "preaching." Jack preached this A.M. on "What is that to thee- Follow though me." good- I taught Nette's S.S. class. She languished at home. Evening Service - John talked on Matt. 6:- Be not anxious" +c
Monday 26. Took train at 11:27 for Chicago + DesMoines. Letter fr. Harold this morning- telegraphed him in Chicago- Dell Hinds sat in front of me on train with his little 4 yr old boy. Ate lunch twice in P.M. Chicago at 9. Harold at train. We had

title: Marion Metcalf diary [10], 1892-1901
transcription:
supper at Hotel- oyster stew + prairie chicken. Train again at 10. Lower Berth 8 on Sleeping Car Eton. berths all made up. Warm weather-
Tues. 27. Beautiful warm day. too warm. Reached DesMoines at 8:20 A.M. Reception Com. at train. Mr. Pease spoke to me. Went to the church. Dr. Frisbie took me + my trunk to Mrs. McFarland's in his carriage. Thither soon came Harl. Meeting began at 2 this afternoon. Mrs. Noble is here at Mrs McFarlands also. Mary arrived at 8:45 this evening. Harl and I met her at the station + took her back to the Reception at the church for a little while- Letter home + to Miss Arnold-
Wed. 28. Still warm, but cloudy. Mr McFarland took us for a drive, out on Grand Avenue. back in time for the meeting. Mary + I went to dinner at the Settlement with Harl. Meetings in afternoon and evening. Saw Gertrude Willcox. 
Thurs. 29 A little cooler + rainy. Meetings all day, as ever. It rained in the afternoon. Went to R.R. office with Mrs Noble.
Fri. 30 Cloudy still + cooler. Mrs Noble started off. at 7 A.M. for Kidder, Mo. to visit her daughter. Mary + I stayed at home all the morning, I on bed much. In P.M. I went with Harl to hear Miss Annie Howe talk to the kindergarten teachers at

title: Marion Metcalf diary [10], 1892-1901
transcription:
the Grant Schoolhouse. Went with Harl to Y.W.C.A. to call on Mrs. Augie Hatton Hurmel, and to look up Mary Stewart, Christian Scientist, WWelleley 87(?) found neither of them in. Went, Mary + I, to Mrs Finsley's to tea. and then with Harl to hear I'm Maclaren at the Opera House- lecture on Scottish Traits - 1 Sense of Humor, not wit" (French) not drollery (Irish- invented - intellect standing on its head.) not fun (English.) but dry humor.
2. Caution- "canny F Scot." never willing to make an admission. "If it hands on as it is now, it threatens to be wet by night"- "More a bit litigious." Scottish clerks do I's + cross t's- become partner in 10 yrs.
3. Dourness - obstinacy raised to the nth power- very few Scottish martyrs- I won't.  4. Sentiment. Reading from McClure + Drumsheugh- Defense of himself from criticisms on Jamie Soutar + Post- He knew 4 Maclurs- thinks there were about 40, of whom he has heard. The London physician in Story of a Servant Lass, in Auld Lang Syne, he knew, + it is the one unvarnished fact in either book. 
Harl came with us up to Mrs McFarland's + found the freezer, with pineapple ice therein. We ate some with crackers, then to bed about 11:30.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [10], 1892-1901
transcription:
Sat. 313. Colder and clear. Flag Day in DesMoines. Went to State House in A.M. + to top of dome. Took lunch at Y.W.C.A.
Roast Beef + gravy 5
Baked Potatoes 3
Turnip 3
Bread. 2 slices 2
Butter 1
Grapes 1
Miss Stever, Miss Jones, Miss Hughes-
In P.M. went in McFarland carriage to call on Mrs Horatio Hall, in North DesMoines. Mrs Watson + Miss Turner called on Mary + me. Read Advance and Iowa State Register on Dan Maclaren.
Republican Parade in evening. Mrs. McF. Mary, Harl + I saw it all from Dr. Cannon's window. Bicycles, old soldiers, Traveling men, R.R. men, Express Co. Scandinavian Club, Hebrew Club, Colored Club, Business Men's +c +c. Fireworks all along also. Home about ten. 
Sunday Fair weather. Church, 10:30. 
Nov. 1 Dr. Frisbie preached on "The Lord hath need of him." We went to Mrs Frisbie's S.S. class. Lesson on The Building of the Temple. Dinner at Settlement, with Harl, Mrs Lynde + Miss Scott. Mary + I lay down for a half hour or so. Junior Endeavor Meeting at 6. Then Mary + I went to Dr Frisbie's with Harl. to crackers + milk +ct - a delightful evening. Prayers at the McFarland's + bed.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [10], 1892-1901
transcription:
Monday - Cloudy morning. Mary
Nov. 2. took 7 AM. train for Kansas City + Lawrence. Harl and I both saw her off.
Ticket . Elyria to DesMoines. 19.20
Popcorn                                          .05
In DesMoines
Carfares                                         .15
Ticket. Desmoines to Elyria   6.40
Ch. Collection                                .10
S.S.                                                  .05
Harl came round here this AM + we had a good visit. Then went to call on Mrs Rawson + on Mary Stewart, Christian Science Physician. then to dinner with Harl at Settlement, + to office to get my ticket home + engage Sleeper. Mrs McFarland and I went out to the Hyland's, at Oak Park to tea - then to Sunbeam Missions, to the close of the Ch. Meeting, then Harl came home with me, and we had a nice visit while Mr + Mrs McFarland went to birthday party.
Called with Harl at Mrs Crawford's. Mrs Cole called here, also Miss Hogan.
Tues. 3. Went to ride in AM. out to the Baggs' district. made call there. tried to see Mr Joseph Hall again. Went with Harl to dinner at Mrs Crawford's. Calle at Mrs. Bowen's with Mrs MrFarland in P.M. then went with Harl + Miss Belle Hunt to see Foot Ball Game between East and West

title: Marion Metcalf diary [10], 1892-1901
transcription:
High Schools. a cool afternoon. Harl came up in the evening + we went to train. 9.30. A Mr. West on same car (Burmah) friend of Harl's. Went soon to bed. Election Day.
Wed. Nov. 4. Chicago. 8:10 A.M. found Miss Mabel Frisbie on car early. sat together mostly till we reached Chicago. Sat nothing of Harold. Wrote letter to Mary + card to Harl in station. Had oyster stew for breakfast about 10 A.M. Train for Elyria, 10:30. Rainy all day. Wrote letter to Dora Freeman on train. Elyria, 6.50 Pater, John, Carrie, Nette, Ely, there to meet me, with Belle + wagon. Found everything apparently all right at home. 
Sleeping Car. D.M. to Chicago.     2.00
Oysters Stew                                        25
Chicago Record                                     01
Thurs.5 Warm, pleasant weather in A.M. Very windy and blustering in P.M. John, Harry, Mays, Nette, Ely + I went to prayer meeting. Pater did not go out. Teachers meeting afterward. Very few present.
Friday 6. Tried to give my report at Missionary Meeting in afternoon. John + Carrie drove over to Oberlin. J.C. Nette + I called at Mrs Fay's in evening.
Sat. 7. Studied S. S. lesson. Mended +c. sweeping + dusting. Saw Dr Sherwood about Nelson. 
Sunday. 8. All went to church except Carrie Franklin + Nelson. John preached on Isaiah 6 - "the vision of God." I taught Mrs Smith

title: Marion Metcalf diary [10], 1892-1901
transcription:
class. Louise [[Brannan?]], Hallie Clough, Mabel Bullock, Miss [[Winson]]. John taught Mrs Cavert's class.
Went to church in evening +or C.E. meeting long enough to speak of the S.S. Convention in Oberlin this week. John spoke on Remembering God + hallowing His name. Family letter + one to Harold.
Monday. 9 Cold, rough day. Nette went to Oberlin at 4:08 to spend the week. Miss Phipps and I called at Mrs. Tucker's and Mrs Hart's to look up the Bell girls for Sunday School. Went to Worker's Training Class at M. E. Ch. in evening. chapel was locked, cold + dark but we broke in and had the meeting. Republican Parade, Jollification. Bessie Brooks walked home with me. Nette went to Oberlin on 4:08 train. 
Tues. 10 Pater went to Oberlin on 11:27 train. John drove over with Dr Sherwood very soon after dinner. Harry went at 5:30. [[Dorce?]] came back. Rain in evening. Warmer. Furnace Fire. Slept in Pater's bed. 
Wed. 11. Went to Oberlin at 11:27 myself - back at 5:07. Pater + Harry still staying. Nelson seems a little better. John, Carrie + I went down to Aunt Anna's in evening- Lamb chops, Gingerbread Pudding-
Thurs. 12- Beautiful weather - warmer + clear. Pater + Harry came home on 9:10 train. Dr Sherwood came up to see

title: Marion Metcalf diary [10], 1892-1901
transcription:
Nelson in A.M. - quinine.
Roast Lamb, Potatoes, Fried Squash, Friend Apple Cooky + custard pudding - Pear Sauce for supper. 
Prayer meeting + Teachers' Meeting. 
Friday. 13. Cloudy. Snowstorms in P.M. C.E. Supper and Social. Harry + Ely, with caps + aprons, helped serve. Mays helped in afternoon. Meeting of Ex. Com. of F.M.Svc. at 2:30 - discussed Junion C. E. + Little Helpers. 
Social. supper            .25
Candy                             10
Popcorn Balls - 2 doz. 20
Sat. 14. Sweeping + dusting. Fried Pork, Cheese Fondu. Cabbage, Baked Potatoes, Gravy. Popcorn balls, Candy -
Miss Brown, Miss Durley, and Nette came at 5:07. Ely + John met them at station. Popovers for supper. Possum Cereal. Crabapple marmalade. Candy pull in evening. Mrs Benton + Marion came over also.
Sun. 15. Beautiful weather. warm and bright. All to ch. except John, Nelson, Franklin + the suffering Ely. Rev. C.A. Vincent of Sandusky preached. A.M. "Why I am a Christian" 1 Cor. 1 20-22. The View of God- Atonement for Sun. P.M. "He that loseth his life for my sake shall find it." He led the C.E. Meeting also.
Mon. 16 Still the Indian Summer continues. Miss Brown + Miss Durley returned to Oberlin on 7:50 train, Nette + John going with them to station. Mays + I went to the Library in ever-

title: Marion Metcalf diary [10], 1892-1901
transcription:
ning to look up references for Ely's debate on Political Parties. Dinner. Chicken Fried Apples. Potato. Apple Pie + Cream. 
Nelson seems much better. Minnie went home sick on Wednesday after making bread. Her mother came, and took her in wagon. She came back Friday, in time to set bread again, but we made none this time. Made 6 pumpkin pies Saturday, Nov. 21. Minnnie did, I mean. Chicken for Sunday Dinner. 
Sunday. 22. John preached on Paul. I did not go. Went only to S. S. and C. E. meeting, at which latter I gave some report from DesMoines. 
Monday - Cloudy. clothes did not dry very well.
Tuesday. Bread baked. 
Wed. A+A + children + Florence Putname came at 5:09 P.M. 3 mince pies, 2 layer cakes, many nutates + chocolate caramels made this day - also turkey stuffed + steamed + potatoes pared for tomorrow. 
Thurs. 26. Thanksgiving Day. Mrs Fay + Ralph came also to dinner _ + Rich's + Sutcliffe's in evening - Popcorn, grapes + pulled candy. A little singing. While thee I seek, Lead, Kindly Light _ +c.
we went to church from this house.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [10], 1892-1901
transcription:
our church. Remarks by Mr. Knapp, Reeder, Fields, Levagood. 
Friday. 27. [[Florence?]] went at 7:50 A</ Azariah took same train for Bucyrus, to a Teacher's Institute. Annie + the babies stayed here - Azariah returned Saturday just at dinner time. Azariah + France went back to Oberlin 7:50 A. M Monday- Annie + baby at 11:27.
Sunday. 29. John preached on "Jesus Christ the same yesterday + today _ forever." Very good indeed.
Taught Mr. Burrows S. S. class. 4 boys present- P.B, S.H. T.F. F.W.
Monday. 30 John had letter fr. Dr. Bead, appointing him to position at Talledega. He + Carrie took 11:27 train for Oberlin, to pack up things, leaving Franklin here. Back at 7:57. Peter sick in the night. 2 AM.
Tues. Dec. 1. J+ C. packing all day.- fortnightly for Nette.
Wed. Dec. 2. J =1.475 ft lb C + frandlin tried to leave at 7:15 AM. left actually at 10:05, from C.L. + W. station. for Talladega, via Columbus, Cinn, Chattanooga +c - lonesome. Table small. Pater went to Sandusky. 8. back at 12.
Thurs. 3. Prayer meeting + Teachers Meeting - Rev. Mc. Cadmus of Hingham, Mass. visiting at A. L. Garford's gave Prep Lectur - Nette + I went

title: Marion Metcalf diary [10], 1892-1901
transcription:
downtown + looked at Holiday Cards at Lersch's. Fair weather. 
Friday - 4 - Missionary Meeting at Mrs J.T. Brooks' _ social time after program- tea + wafers + candy. Mrs. Hamilton went, but not Mrs LeMaster- Geo Rich brought a whole hog here_ Nelson much better nowadays-, but not at school as yet. A little snow.
Sat. 5. Mince pies made and stuffing for roast meat for tomorrow also apple sauce in plenty.
Down town in P.M. to Philpott + Daniell's over to Aunt Mallie's- Swept rather extensively upstairs + dusted less so- Miss Mattie Hulbert sewed here Thurs. + Friday - bound carpet, mended Keyes' waist, fixed waists + black skirt for Nette- paid her $1.10.
Subscriptions - Life + Light   60
                            Dayspring        20
Dec. 3. 2 fr. slippers.              1.50
                  Shoestrings               10
                          Donkeys +c        25
                    Saxony yarn            20
                        Thread                  12
Sunday. Dec. 6. Stayed at home from church with Nelson and went late to Sunday School. Communion Sunday. Mr. Cadmust preached on Self Sacrifice. Unity of God & Christ. evening on Self Realization, no text. He led the C.E. Meeting

title: Marion Metcalf diary [10], 1892-1901
transcription:
Dinner. Roast Mutton, Potato, Dressing, Gravy. Cranberry Sauce, Pickled Vegetable Peaches. Mince Pie. Harry went to West River Road S.S. with Roy Foley. Male quartet sang "Sanctus" in P.M.
Monday. 7. Nette + Harry went to Oberlin with wagon + a load. Wrote notes to Porter Williams, Carl Foley, Hiram Cerpas +c + a letter to John. H Thurston- Tried to see Miss Monroe. Went to Training Class in evening Called on Mrs Huntington + Bessie Haines.
Tues. 8 Went to see Miss Monroe quite early in morning then looked at stockings +c at Lersch's + Crehore, Fauwer + Robinson's.tried vainly to find Henry Ingersoll, at his office, but caught him at his house just after dinner. Candy pull in evening. Roy Foley, Carl Foley, John + Louise Heck, Fred Dunham, Hiram Cerpas. Thode Fason, Percy Brynton. Arthur Chapman. Candy mostly [[granied?]] ; but tasted good. Bought two Magic Boxes.
Wed. 9 Anna Monroe here in A.M. some confidences about musical matters in our church. Mrs Fay came in P.M. Went to supper at chapel at 6. carrying down our beautiful branch of Japan Quince. Asked Dr Sherwood about Pater_ he says he is not at all well. saw Mayor Levagood also.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [10], 1892-1901
transcription:
Thurs. 10 Mending + S.S. lesson mostly. Prayer meeting in evening - all went - Religious Reading. Mr Cadmus. a full meeting. followed by Teachers' Meeting. 
Miss Hall. Milk         1 00
Mrs French "               05
Friday. 11. Minnie went home, with sore throat, Pater having first taken her down to see Dr. Sherwood - she took the 11:27 train. 
Dinner- Pork Omelet. (?) Potato, Parsnips. Gravy. Poor Man's Pudding with Cream. 
Supper. Oatmeal Cakes. Apple Sauce. Mended Nelson's trousers + blue shirt. Dusted more or less. Warm weather.
Sat. 12 Cooked Pig's Feet. Made Lard. Roasted meat, +c for tomorrow's dinner_ Nette swept much + long- A little meting
Sunday. 13 Mr Cadmust preached on The Manliness of Christ, courage, sincerity, generosity. John 18:8 - evening, "Hallowed be Thy Name"_ All went to ch. + S.S. on time, too. I talked a little to the Primary Sunday School. Warm.
Monday. 14 Beautiful, sunny weather - No Minnie + no washing- she came at 5P.M. Cold spare rib_ pigs' feet. Potao - gravy. celery (cooked-)Coffee Cream, wh. hardened not at all_ Pater _ I went over to Mrs. Garford's Reception in evening - started soon after 6:30. back here about 8:20. Very good time - Crystal Wedding - many appeared in wedding gowns.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [10], 1892-1901
transcription:
Tuesday 15. Rain or snow all day- Sent washing over to Mrs Jackson in A.M. Made Tomato Sauce + Favorite Pudding. Lay on lounge much. Committee meeting with Mrs Chapman at Mrs Benton's in PM.
Wed- 16 Oysters- Minnie seems improving-
Thurs. 17 Prayer meeting had no leader till 7:15 nearly. then Mr Schaible - very few at Teachers' Meeting. Nette went to Oberlin at 4:08, to hear the Messiah this evening - Oysters for breakfast-
Fri. 18. Took Nelson downtown with me after school, for a little Christmas shopping- Went to Library with Nette in evening- Mending - 
Sat. 19. Mending. Baked Beans for dinner, + cold spare rib_ Tearing off Paper
Sunday. 20 Clear + cold. Bro. Bosworth preached in A.M. fr. "He that is greatest among you shall be your servant." Evening _ Song Service by Elyrian Male Quarter. Sanctus, Eccl. 12. Still, Still with Thee. Prof. B. spoke on "Presence of God + Acquaintance with God-" Harry, Ely + I went to Jail in afternoon_
Monday. 21 May + Harry, Nette + I tore off paper in dining room. I worked only in P.M. Did not finish the job today - Went to see Anna Monroe in A.M. about the Christmas Entertainment.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [10], 1892-1901
transcription:
Tues. 22 Snowstorm- Finished getting off paper about 11 A.M. Harry painted part of ceiling in P.M. Mrs Fay came to consult about the Missionary Meeting Sunday evening. Went to see Mary Parker, Belle Fason + to Republican and Democrat offices-
Musser Hose- 2 pr. for Harl.      1.00
Hairbrush                                          25
Toothbrushes- 2@15                     30
Knitting silk- 2 spools                    25
Wed. 23. More business in preparation for S.S. Christmas. Slides arrived-
Thurs. 24. Went with May in A.M. to woods for evergreens. Belle very lively- Miss Brown came at 5:07 train half br. late however- Entertainment in evening, said to be very successful- Children did well. Harry sang beautifully 0 "O little town of Bethlehem."
Friday. 25 Christmas Day. Minnie went home at 11:27. Harold came at 11:55. Dinner, Spare rib, Mashed potato + turnip. cranberry sauce, pumpkin pie, nutcase. whipped cream. Candy - Harry Braman sent me a 5 lb. box of very nice candy for Christmas present. Sleighride- Bad cold- early to bed.
Sat- 26. Ely 15 years old. No Minnie, Marguerite Upton came in AM + Went to Cleveland on 3:30 car- Nette + Harold went over to the cemetery-

title: Marion Metcalf diary [10], 1892-1901
transcription:
Venison for dinner-
Sun. 27. Did not go out all day. Got dinner +c. No Minnie- Venison Roast - Grape Jam with whipped cream. Miss Brown taught Mr Burrow's class. Mr. Milton Norton preached. Missionary Meeting in evening, conducted by Mrs Hay, but I went not- Nette at home in evening too
Monday.28. Miss Brown took 7:50 train back to Oberlin- Minnie came last night at 5:30- Went to Oberlin with Harold. started about 10 A.M. - back about 3:30 P.M. dinner at Annie's. A beautiful, bright day- Harold left for Chicago 7:50 P.M. 
Tues. 29 Did some Christmasing- made calendars + did up things- Pitched in to mending also.
Wed. 30 Continued - mending finished actually-
Thurs. 31. Annie, France + bag came at 9:10_ Azariah at 5 - very bad weather. foggy - Prayer meeting + teachers meeting in evening.
Friday - Jan. 1- 1897

title: Marion Metcalf diary [10], 1892-1901
transcription:
P'd Fanny Bratton-
Jan 14-            $1.50
Bread - for wk- .66
Monday, Jan 18 0 Bread.            .24
Shirts. Ely.     2@ 50                  1.00
Mayo-                                               50
Trousers- Keyes-                           50
Went to see Mrs Flickenger, Mrs Bowen, Rev. F.C. Eldred. Zada Crisp here in evening to see about going to Geo Rich's tomorrow to surprise party-
Fues. Jan. 19. Surprise party for Geo Rich's in evening. choir invited. George's wagon, driven by Mr Jones, carried up 15 or so. Harry with our wagon took Miss Monroe, Pearl Hoyt, Clara Rittenberg + me. Geo was completely surprised. had been at Farmer's Institute in Ridgeville all day, as had also Pater.
Oil barrel filled Monday, Jan 18.
Tues. Jan. 19.    Bread                                   35
Thurs. 21.                 "                                       24
Fri. 22                                                                08
Washing + Ironing - Ling Hing (Pater)    1.50
     "            Mrs_______ (Fisherville)           65
Union Suits- flannel. self. 2@ 1.35 (ch.) 2.70
Thurs. 21. Went to Oberlin at 11:27, back at 5:07. to see Mrs. Parmelee about coming to Missionary Meeting in Elyria - carried clothes to Mayo + brought clothes back. Little Marion is lovely -
Began on Tues. Jan. 19 to teach Ralph Fay Latin (Caesar) - an hour 4 days in week.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [10], 1892-1901
transcription:
Tues. to Fri.
Pater was sick- one of his attacks - Friday Jan 22. 4:30A.M. Minnie came on 5:07 train Thursday evening, Jan. 20 - cam out on train with me from Obelin, is to stay here till she finds another place. Mrs Ely p'd on Sat. Jan 15 .90 up to date + 2 1/2 its over + above. Mrs Brooks began to take milk Wed.
Jan 13. 4 qts. p'd.
Thurs. 14. 1 qt. Monday. 18. 1 q't.
Tues. 19    1
Wed. 20    1

Review Day in S.S. I gave some general questions at opening 10 minutes perhaps.

Monday Nov. 4 back on morning train.  Dinner - Codfish, Potatoes, 2 kinds Chocolate Mauge Fruit.  Mrs. Strauss called in P.M.  Went with Ely to Local Union Social in G.A.R Hall. 2 solos, 3 declarations, and a Library of 30 books - home 10 P.M.  9 letters.

Mrs. Fred Smith & Miss Ann Monroe called while we were gone. 5 letters. Mended Keyes' trousers & hosen. Miss Wadsworth here.

Wed. 6 Miss Wadsworth. Chickens for dinner, celery, potatoes, fruit. Meeting of Fortnightly. Funeral of Mrs. E.S. Nichols yesterday. Marriage of Geo. Lee and Katherine Heal tonight. Went late to chapel to supper talk with Miss Fisher and Mrs. Brooks.

Went to library after dinner and got 3rd volume of Mortey in wh. I have read some. Progressed in acquaintance with Miss Willard . she is a Boston [[?]] - teacher -, and I appear to like her. We are going to read some together. she has loaned me "Titus, a comrade of the Cross."

Wed. 8 Warmed - 10o above - took quite a walk after prayers. Read Mortey + knitted - wrote letter to Cohas.
Salt rub at 9:45 + rest thereafter. Went to see Dr. Thayer after dinner,

title: Marion Metcalf diary [09], 1892-1901

Service in evening. Lecture by Mr Adams on Jesus Christ as a teacher. authoritative, without argument, [[?]]casurial. of unique Majesty -

Wed. 9 - Butter - 4 lbs.   100

title: Marion Metcalf diary [08], 1892-1901
transcription:
Pastor's Room - Went to Poorhouse in afternoon. Miss Moore, Langford and W.H. Harris. old people very glad to see us. back at 3:15 - Did not go to church, being somewhat tired - Normal Class S.S. teachers not Seniors, here at the Cottage at 5. somewhat successful. but not all here - Prayers in evening, short. In bed at 9.
Monday -16- Cooler - clear - 2 good bicycle rides - and a walk to Hampton with Miss Moore. Bible Class, & History Examination in evening - Bed before 10. Letter to Nette. Letter from home, enclosing John's first from Berlin-
Tues. 17 No frost, last night, though expected - No Junior Bible Class, though also expected. Papers came which Chas had sent from Perry, Oklahoma - in Cherokee Strip - A's & D's in A.M. Literature (Poor Richard) and Algebra in evening - Myrtilla and Miss Moore dropped in during the Algebra - Bed just as taps finished - Bicycle Ride, and meet with stern disapproval from old man.
Wed. 18. No bicycle today - bed most of P.M. School sang the 20 min fr. 9-9:20, so I have not yet seen my Junior Bible Class. All went to chapel in evening - Batallion officers read & fire duty assignments, & some

title: Marion Metcalf diary [08], 1892-1901
transcription:

title: Marion Metcalf diary [08], 1892-1901
transcription:
School year - '94-'95 - Hampton -
Left home Thurs. Sep. 27, 9:10 A.M. reached Cleveland at 10. [[?]] met me at station - home with her to 427 Clark Ave, where I had a nice little visit, a glimpse of their new church, and a good dinner - Train at 1:40 for Pittsburgh - Supper from lunchbox in station at P. Sleeper Rialto at 8:10 for Washington. Bed about 9. no watch. Washington 7:50 A.M. on Friday - found 215 Pa. Ave. S.E. and Mrs. Kellogg, Miss Goodwin and Miss Lockhart all right - a good breakfast & wash. Saw Monument, Bureau of Printing & Engraving, Treasury, Capitol & outside of White House. Boat at 7 P.M.  found Miss Booth and Miss Lowe thereon. Stateroom 34 - Steamer Washington  - Old Pt. about 6:15 A.M. in a pouring rain. Electric cars over to school - Coffee &c at 7: sharp.
Saturday. Sept. 29. Rain all day. got boxes down in A.M. & unpacked trunk in P.M. - curtains up re-sent postal card home - Letter from Ethel & papers - Chapel in evening - very tired.
Sunday. Sep. 30 - Clouds, but little rain

title: Marion Metcalf diary [08], 1892-1901
transcription:
Hush, my babe, be still and slumber. 
Holy angels guard thy bed.
Heavenly blessings without number,
Gently falling on thy head.
How much better thou'rt attended,
Than the Son of God could be,
When from heaven He descended,
And became a child like thee.
Soft and easy in thy cradle,
Coarse and hard thy Saviour lay,
When his birthplace was a stable,
And his softest bed was hay.
Oh, to tell the wondrous story,
How His Foes abused their King.
How they killed the Lord of glory,
Makes me angry while I sing.
Hush, my child, I did not chide thee,
Thought my song may seem so hard,
'Tis thy mother sits beside thee, 
And her arms shall be thy guard.
May'st thou learn to know and fear Him
Love and serve Him all thy days;
Then to dwell forever near Him,
Tell His love and sing His praise.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [07], 1892-1901
transcription:
School Year- 1892-3-

Sep. 29. Started from home 12:17 P.M. with Ranusky- ticketed and checked for Washington, D.C. The 4 small boys had all gone to the County Fair, so I did not see them to say Goodby.  Uncle Herbert went to Cleveland on same train. Tran was late, and we had just time to find our other train in Cleveland. 1:40 on the Pennsylvania R.R.  Took sleeper at Pittsburgh at 8:10 for Washington. Miserable headache. Sent card home from Pittsburgh.

Sep. 30, Friday. Washington about 8 A. M.  A beautiful morning. Had baggage re-checked at station, then went to wharf to leave packages & luggage stateroom for tonight. Then Ramsey & I ate breakfast from our lunch boxes and went through the Botanical Gardens to the Capitol.  want about there, then to Nat'l. Museum, where we met Miss Moor & Mr. Lade.  
Very tired. I went to wharf for my bag, had tea & toast at station & sat there all the afternoon. sent card home. Miss Booth & Lavinia Cornelius came into station while I was there, on their way to Hampton. On the boat I found Miss Johnston. We all had staterooms near together. I had supper on the boat, as our lunch boxes were lost. found John L. Brown, of last year's Hampton class, a waiter in the dining room there.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [07], 1892-1901
transcription:
Oct. 1. Saturday. Landed at Old Point about 6:30 A.M. Miss woodward, Miss Showers, Miss Felitham, Mr. Goodrich, Mr. Small were at the wharf. also Urquhart with a carriage.
Breakfast at 8, tasted good. Miss Nettleton not yet here, but room was ready. Got boxes over from Virginia Hall in A. M. & unpacked.
Lay on bed or lounge considerable. sent card home. Trunk did not come. was carried on to Norfolk by some blunder. Went to bed at 8. with Miss Lowe's nightdress. Very warm.

Oct. 2. Sunday.  Cool-but lovely weather.
Went to Bucknore Sunday School & taught the older people, 3 of them. S.S. here was only general [[?]]. Bed most 7 p.M. Miss Foote came in, also Mrs. Turner and the children. Wrote letter home. read Miss. Review, Faber's Hymns, & Bible. Went to Wigwam after supper to sing. Bed about 9.

Oct. 3. Monday.  Trunk came in A.M. Proceeded to unpack. Miss Nettleton did not arrive as expected, but came at night, about 7:30.  Meeting with Mr. Friscel & other teachers of Pastor's class, at 10, after wh. Mr. Junner, Miss Lowe & I continued the consultation. 
Met miss Hyde after dinner, and she asked me to have general charge of bright Middlers. Went down to the Dixie after prayers in evening, with Miss Woodward. found Miss Connacher in bed. Back at 9, and found Miss Nettleton in the room, unpacking.  
Bed about 10. A cool day.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [07], 1892-1901
transcription:
Oct. 4. Tuesday- Warmer. Day School met at 9 but no classes. I helped give out books all the morning. Miss Moore, arrived this morning, also Dora Freeman.
Moved in P.M. to serve esthist, over to Tom's cottage. Night School was not called together this evening, as there were more examinations to be given.  Began letters to Harl. put up desk curtains & e.

Oct. 5. Wednesday.  Cool, except in middle of day. Letter from home. A Middle Bible Class at 11:20, a delightful class only 11 members at present. Tried to get ready for Night Middlers in afternoon. taught them Anth. & Hist. in evening.

Thurs. 6. Very cool. we had wood fire all day, and steam in the evening.  A Middlers in A. M. 4 new ones, 3 of the N. J. Indians.
Prayer meeting in evening, all together, very good. Pastors Class Teachers Meeting, al
2. difficulty in making schedule.
only 2 periods in evening, History, & A Jr. Bible.
my first sight of the A. Juniors. Letter to Harl.

Friday, 7  Cool still. Myrtilla took my Middlers in the evening for an hour, after which I prepared them a little for Jenny's evening & then did Mental Arith. A Juniors, the last period.  Started, & sent Family letter. Read Tennyson before goiog to bed.  Changed seat at table.

Sat. 8.  Fine weather. raining in night. class at 11:20. Went rowing with Miss Mary Clarke in P.M. Bath at Va. Hall. clothes ready for

title: Marion Metcalf diary [07], 1892-1901
transcription:
Laundry at Griggs Hall- did nothing in evening, with Miss Moore assistance.

Sunday-9. Cloudy in A.M. Cleared. Cool.  
Sunday School. Opening exercises with Seniors who rather terrified me. before my own class came down. Very little time for the lesson. Went to church in P.M. Bad cold.

Monday. 10.  Fine, cool, clear weather.  
Went over to the Fort with Myrtie and her friends, Mrs. Allen & Miss Norton, in A. M. Teacher's Meeting at 4. Letters to Ethel. & KIry Foster.
Tennyson, in Night School, with Middlers- 7:30 to 8:20 or so. then gymnastics- No class for me the last period. My A Juniors evidently had first 3 instead of last 3.

Tues. 11.  Lovely weather. warmer. Pastor's class began, only 2 in 1st Div. price and Freeman.  9 in 2nd, an inspiring class, especially the Indian Patterson.  6 different lessons to prepare for Night School-rather distracting- 2 histories, 2 arithmetics,  current events, Bible lesson. Took a walk in P. M. 

Wed. 12. Cloudy all day- warmer. Up at 6. Early breakfast. Letters from home, Nette, Georgine Fraser, W. C. '90.  9 lessons again, but got along better than yesterday. Walk with Dora.

Thurs. 13. Fine weather. Went to walk with Misses Moore, Nettleton, and Adamms to Soldiers

title: Marion Metcalf diary [07], 1892-1901
transcription:
Home, and around by the Dixie. Night School dismissed about 8, as the gas was so very poor. Prayer meeting for Night Girls led by Miss Lorne- Very many there, but very few took part. Letter from Kiry Foster. Wrote letters home to Georgine Frazer. ordering Week's Current & stopping Public Opinion.

friday. 14.  Letters to Wilder, Fern Smith and Rollin Reefy. Made papers to be printed for Pastor's Class, on Inspiration of the Bible, Revised Versions re.
Went rowing with Dora, Miss MOore & Miss Nettleton. read Review of Reviews with Miss Booth and Miss Lowe.  No Night School, poor gas.

Saturday. 15.  Lovely weather, much warmer.  Letters to Nette and Marion Marsh. 
Only one class, at 11:20 - Bath at Va. Hall in P. M.  Walked to Hampton with Misses Moore and Nettleton. Bought AmCl 10, and sponge 10 for inkbottle.  Went at 5 to read Review of Reviews to Miss Booth & Miss Louse. read about Whittier and Geo. Wm. Curtis.  Mended clothes. Read of Homestead Strike, in N. A. Rev. & Forum.

Sunday, 16.  Prayer meeting at 8:20. Spoke very briefly. Sunday School, some good.
Went to Slabtown in P. M. but had no class.  Don went to Shellbanks after church, & Miss Nettleton came to stay with me.  Misses Scoville, Showers, Moore & Nettleton came over after supper.

Monday. 17.  Early breakfast. Most of A.M. in Library. Rowing in P.M. with Myrtie and w. Miss Lowe.  2 classes in evening.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [07], 1892-1901
transcription:
"I pledge allegiance to my Flag" - re- 
Letter from Ethel & Jas. E. Beeman
buried.

Tuesday - 18.  Water famine very m[[?]]nant.  Girls washed dishes in cold salt water this morning.  Work Day for A Middle Class, as I had no class this A. M. 
Rowing with Don & Miss Lowe in afternoon.
Proofs of Bible paper came-

Wed. 19.  Fine weather, the needed rain has not arrived.  All my classes today, with reasonable success. 
Read Caesar to Lyle, Thompson, & Sykes. 
Letter from home. Week's Current came today. 30 copies, 2 members- 60 papers.

Thurs. 20.  Warm & fair  Eclipse came off as advertised this P. M.  Led Night girls prayer meeting, very many told when they became Christians.  Read about Homestead Strike in N. A. Review, to Middlers.
Wrote letter home. Went out rowing iwth Miss Scoville in the "Isabel"

Friday, Oct. 21.  Columbus Day. Breakfast at 7:30 instead  of 8. Celebration began at 9:15. We all pledged allegiance to our flag with some Veterans from the "home" to help us, then exercises in the church. 
In P.M. the students had an entertainment in the chapel, some good, some not to. 
Ballgame also. Read aloud to Dora the chapter on 13th Cent. in White's 18 Christian Centuries, wh. we very greatly enjoyed.
Sociable in Gymnasium in evening.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [06], 1883-1889
transcription:
Note. Carrie Pierce went to live at Miss Townsends'. Mrs. Stevens and I escorted her thither after dinner. I had a little run with Wallace- Snow.

Thurs. 28 Classes 9, 1:30, 3:10 - Came over h[[?]] for Lunch. Note Books few. House begins to look habitable. Hung my pictures. Studied Bible lesson. Miss [[?]] and Mrs. Stevens not well. Had colds. Wrote letter home.

Fri. March comes in like a lamb. beautiful.

Mar. 1 spring like weather. First bible class for me at 2:20. Chemistry Quiz 9 and 3:10. Went to prayer meeting in Village with Mrs. Newton. Preparatory Lecture.

Sat. 2 Lovely weather. Went to Boston at 8:15. tried to get ticket for Lowell Sustitute Course. Prof. Ed-ward Morse. Stood 1 1/2 hrs. in rain. Went to Mr. [[?]]'s [[?]] Temple Class in P.M. came out at 4:50 - Rose and Ring in Gymnasium for Chapel Fund - did not go - Mended a little, read B[[?]] Ballads with Miss Holmes. Made out lesson on Ba[[]] for Bible class - Katherine Fisher is to go to the college Monday.

Sun. Mar. 3 Cloudy, clearing for a little in afternoon. Went to church and S.S. taught my S.S. class. Mr. McCabe and [[?]] Gr[[?]] only being present. In after-noon, went to talk with Miss Kendall and Miss Vancl[[?]]de. 2 missing meetings in the evening.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [06], 1883-1889
transcription:
Dr. Wilcox preached at the college in the morning.  Miss. 
Meeting in the afternoon.  Dr. Holbrook of China (a lady).  
Mon.  Letter to Patrons.  Filed our application blank
for Teachers' ______ Association.  Went to walk
in afternoon with _______ _________ Lecturer at College
in evening by Professor Smith of Columbia.  did not
go.  Party in Miss Bliss & Leavitt's room this
evening.  Inauguration Day.  Rain in Wash-
ington.  Clouds here.  Sent book to Ethel.
Tues. 5.  Rain & mud.  Classes as usual.
At College from 8AM to 10PM.  Note Books as
well as classes.  Faculty Meeting in evening.
Morning silent time voted down.  & Rode
back with K.L. Bates.  Letters from Pater, and
the mither & Ethel.
Wed. 6.  Letters from Lilla D.P. with photo of
King Arthur & from Mrs. Booth, suggesting
that we make a contribution to her work in N.Y.
City.  Cong. Life from Jack.  Classes 1:30 and 2:20
Note Books thereafter.  Wrote letters to Ethel &
Jack. Saw people about Mrs. Booth's letter.
Rain all day.  Deep mud.  Rubber boots.
Thus. 7.  Letter from Ethel.  Classes as usual.  Note Books
also.  Wrote letter home.  And one to Edith.
Went to college in evening to hear Miss Patrick from 
the _________ Home School.  Business Meeting
of Christian Association afterwards fro 5 minutes or so.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [06], 1883-1889
transcription:
"The Rivals", given in Gymnasium, for benefit of "Students Aid Society" - none of us went.

Sunday Mar 24.  Lovly spring day again - Rev. Geo. C. Adams, of Holliston, Mass. preached - Isa. 5:20 " Woe unto them that call evil good & good evil".

Rev. Father Endeavor Clark preached at College _ "We know not what we shall be." Katherine Fisher here for dinner_ also Miss Jenkins. Went to Y.P. Meeting in evening with Miss Harward. had supper after we came back. Finished "We Two". Rob't Anderson back. at S. S. today. very brown.

Monday 25 lewler[?] some clouds & wind. Went to station & to college in A.M. to consult about Dr. Schaufflers' coming here. Saw C.F.R. and her sister and Caius Cousins. need papers. Wrote to Jack, Wilder. Dr. Schauffler and M.S. Waton. Made calls in P.M. on Mrs.  Cowan [?], Mrs. Sanborn [?], Mrs. Dana, Miss Winsor, & the Townsends.   ate [?] first two with Mrs Newton. Piano Recital at College in evening, by Miss O'Brien. Things arrived from Teachers' [?] Ass. Welcomed my watch back again. Postal from Uncle George. Rose Terrylerber's[?] "Steadfast" from Mr Cowan. began same in evening.

Tues. 26 Classes at 9 & 1:30. Did Note Books nearly all the rest of the day. About 50 Note Books. Lunch at College & late for dinner. Mended stockings & read "Steadfast" in evening. Geo. W. Cable read in the church in the village - free to all, by liverality of the Misses Eastman. All the girls went from this house. 

Wed 27 Wrote to Uncle Geo. Pater & Ethel. Finished "Steadfast" & went to Mr Cowan's [?] to return it.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [06], 1883-1889
transcription:
Tues.16. Cloudy most of day--Beautiful morning--classes as usual. Did Note Books & Problems. 2:20-4. Went to see Abby. Went over to Mrs [[Cowan's?]] to tell Miss Roberts could not sing at the Temperance Convention. Wrote to Boston Advertiser to ask about political meetings, [[unclear]] Cassius and I. 
Faculty Meeting in evening--rode back with Dr. Barker, & Katherine (and Mr. Bigelow)
Wed. 17 Carried black dress over to Emma [[Vannicy?]] in A.M. Classes in P.M. - as usual. Letter from home this evening-
Letter from Mrs. Booth in A.M.
Thurs.18 Classes all day. Papers from Mrs. Booth in A.M. - Photographs of herself, Marshall Booth, and the baby, came in evening mail--Miss Pendleton and Miss Hawes were here for dinner--Wrote letters home to Mrs. Booth, to Hon. John W. Candlen for list of Republican meetings. 
Fri. 19. Did not go up to College at all--on bed most of day. Dr. Barker came in A.M. to see Maggie, and gave me some pills also. Read Lucy Crofton--and the Salvation Army Literature which came yesterday. M.Marsh & Grace Derry came in, a few minutes in P.M. [[unclear]] Varney brought back my dress. studied S.S. lesson--
Sat. 20 Rode up in A.M. kept Sunday Library - Geology Lecture, 2:20 class. Physical Geography Lecture at 4. by Prof. Niles. Miss [[Cowley?]] and Miss Taylor came down with me to dinner, and staid till halfpast eight.
I went down to the Townsends a few minutes to show them

title: Marion Metcalf diary [06], 1883-1889
transcription:
morning while I was at the College _ Wallace is sick yesterday and today & they _ slept in the kitchen last night, much to his disgust. Miss Kendall came down to see him _
Tues. Rain & wind still continue _ walking almost impossible on Cottage St. Sent letter to Annie. also one to Salvation Army Wa[?]lery_  Classes as usual. Rode down with all family at 4_ Wallace followed us to College this morning_ Letter from Ethel tonight_ Read on Judges_
Wed. 28 No classes. West to Breton [?] at 8:15 and returned at 11. bought Mileage ticket, rubber boots &c_ Fine weather at last_ Walked to Natick in P.M. with Miss Kendall, Miss Leavitt & Wallace_ Misses Graber, Fairbank, McAlaney [?] & Parler went away today for Thanksgiving_ We popped corn & boiled chestnuts this evening. Miss Wiser [?] came in for a little while. Letter from Pale[?] the [miller? mitten? mother?]_
Thurs. 29 Thanksgiving Day_ Rain_ Breakfast at 8. Went to church_ Dinner at 2 at the Eliot. we all spent the evening there also. back a little before 10. Letter from the sursall[?] boys all four_ Wrote letter Louie. May Patterson had a box _ doughnuts & homemade candy_
Friday 30_ Gray day_ some rains_ Wrote to Harry_ Nette{?] Myra J. Hires[?], Gertrude Chandler. Went to College in afternoon_ walk with M. K.K. & Miss Leavitt & Wallace. Prayermeeting in evening_

title: Marion Metcalf diary [05], 1883-1889
transcription: Marion Metcalf - July - 1887

title: Marion Metcalf diary [05], 1883-1889
transcription:
Postal from Miss Eaton-
July-9- Left Elysia- 8 a.m. - for Chautauqua,
with Will Metcalf- Miss Emerson joined us at
Cleveland. A very comfortable journey, though
a warm day- Had to wait 3 hrs. in Brocton- 
reached Chautauqua- 6:10 P.M. Met at land
-ing Miss McElwee, Prof. Ballantine, Prof. Mc
Clintock, Mrs Wriauts + some friends of
Miss Emerson's- Alice Williams + Miss Mary
Williams were on the boat. Supper at Mtn-
air Cottage, where we found Dean Wright +
family, Prof. Knapp of Yale Coll.+ his wife
Prof. Waters + Prof. Reynolds, also of Yale-
Miss Henderson, teacher of woodcarving here-
Mrs King- + of course Miss Neely - Trunks
arrived soon after 9. Miss Emerson + I went
to the Reception very late + for a few minutes -
Sunday-10- A beautiful day, rather cool-
Church. S.S. + Song Service in evening-
Rev. Mark Guy Pease preached, a good sermon
though Prof Knapp +c talked seriously about it 
at dinner. Will + I went to S. S. together-
Lewis Mills conducted it. The Song Service
was the sleepiest I ever attended at Chautauqua
Went to bed early.
Mon. 11. Cool + lovely. Wrote to Mr. McCoy + to Miss
Roberts, mostly before breakfast. A' home letter
after breakfast. Went to morning prayers then

title: Marion Metcalf diary [05], 1883-1889
transcription:
had an interview with Prof. Starr.  Bought a steamer ticket, ink, pens & c. had my watch fixed.  Took my first geological excursion to Jamestown & back this afternoon.  Went rowing [roving?]after supper & for a few minutes to Prof. Cumerock's Reading - Had little talk with Prof. Reynolds.

Tues. 12 Very warm.  Went to morning prayers. to chorus rehearsal with Mss Everson & Mr. Waters. got Atlas of Chautauqua Co. & studied it a little.  Met Prof. Starr at 2.  Went to Social Science (Prof. Richard T. Ely) at 3 - read the paper on Glacial Period in Chaut. Lake Region - read also a little German.  Miss E & I rowed to Point ??? & back to inquire about her box of books.  Letter fr. Mrs. Durant, wh. I sent to Lottie Roberts with a brief letter added.

Wed. 13. Very warm.  Took 7:25 boat for Jamestown & was out all day - till 5:15 P.M.  tracked the Conerango Creek to where it cuts through the solid rock. looked for fossils.  looked at gravel banks???  Mr. Williams & his two daughters were on the boat coming up.  I had quite a visit with him.  Went up to hear the Princeton Glee Club in the evening for a few minutes.  Letter from Pater.

Thurs. 14.  Went to Prof. Starr at 9 and was

title: Marion Metcalf diary [05], 1883-1889
transcription:
ashamed of myself.  Took 11:15 boat to Long Point t0 look at  a railroad cutting.  Very many men looked at me, so that i did not greatly enjoy it. saw the animals. had to stay there until nearly 5 because the Hiawatha broke down over at Bennis Point. Went to Spelling match in the evening but did not spell.  Sent letter home. Very warm in A.M. cooler towards night.

Friday 15.  Went to Prof. Starr at 10,& at 11. & to the Electricity Class fr. 3-5. Rowing in the evening with miss Emerson & Mrs. Org[??] wo arrived today.  Still very warm.

Sat. 16 Took 9:30 boat to Mayville with Prof. Starr, Prof. Boyden, John McGregor & Will Metcalf.  from there by carriage to Hog's Back Ravine, near Westfield on Chautauqua Creek. Then down to Lake Erie at Barcelona - back at 6:10 a very hot day & some hard climbing, but a good time.  Went in evening with Miss Ericson to Reception at the College building - had a good time. Miss Ericson's friends Miss Sumner & Miss Miner arrived at 6:10 - Letter from home - Sent letter to M. March & c.

Sun. 17 Warm still.  Went to church, Sunday School & Even Song Service.  Had a

title: Marion Metcalf diary [05], 1883-1889
transcription:
little talk with Mrs. Fuller & Mr. Fuller - read Bible some. Rev. T. B. Neely preached in the A.M. Dr. Vincent conducted to Song Service & Mr. Corigan spoke briefly.

Mon. 18 Cooler. cloudy window. some rain.  Studied in A.M. Went to Prof. Starr at 11 & staid to his Dynamical Geology Class. After dinner went to the Chem. Lab. to test the efflorescenses we found Saturday.  Then with Will to Pt. Chautauqua to examine the R.R.  cut & to call on Mr. Williams & family both of wh. we did & were late to supper.
Letters from Miss Eaton & Lottie - To bed at 8:00.
Tues. 19.  Warmer. Prof. Starr at 11. & geol. Class 11:30-12:30.  Took boat at 4:00 to Point Chautauqua & walked on R. R. track to Mayville. Found only very small cuts, & some large boulders of guiess & feldspathic rock. Boat was late, so I was very late to supper.  Went in evening to Prof. Riddle's Reading. Wrote to Lottie Roberts, Miss Eaton & Pater.

Wed. 20 Warm again, not to say hot.  Studied in A.M. Class at 11 & 11:30. Went down by the  R.R. station to hunt for fossils in the P.M. with Will. Rain  most of P.M. In evening went rowing, rough & windy - then to Col Sprague's lecture & then to Cong. Social - short letter fr. Ethel -

title: Marion Metcalf diary [05], 1883-1889
transcription:
Thurs. 21 Quiet warm still.  Geology 11-12:30, took a nap after dinner.  Went to Social Science & to Shakspeare Class.  Had a fine row after supper with Miss Everson & her two friends - Letter from Flo Mussey Metcalf - 
Friday 11 Showery.  A hard rain just after dinner.  Went fossil hunting in A.M. out the road gate.  Then to Prof. Starr's lectures on Chautauqua flowers at 11.  Heard Col. Sprague in P.M.  & spoke to him.  Went to Mayville & back by steamer just before supper.  Postal from Miss Eaton.  Wrote letter home.  A row after supper with Mrs. O. Miss E, Miss Minier, Miss Sumner & Miss Burbank left today.

Sat. 23 Went to Panama Rocks.  Last Saturday's party, with the addition of Prof. Gorman - a fine day & fine time.  Back about 6:15.  Pronunciation Match this evening.  Sent letter home.

Sun. 24 Warm & showery - Went to Mr. Holmes bible reading on Peter at 9 & to opening exercises at the Amphitheatre.  Dr. G. W. Miller of Brooklyn preached an educational sermon fr. Prov. 19:2 & Matt. 8:19.
S.S. in P.M.  In the evening we stayed at

title: Marion Metcalf diary [05], 1883-1889
transcription:
house.  Mr. & Mrs. Teller, Miss Emerson & I read the bible and sang hymns, in th. finally nearly all the cottage joined.  Prof. Knapp seemed to enjoy it specially.

Mon. 25.  Rainy all day.  Geology in A.M. lazy in P.M. Went to Dr. Edward's talk on the Physiological Effects of Alchohol at 5.  Some temperance and  inter??? talk with Mr. Reynolds at supper.  Miss Henderson & I called on Lil? Heuermann after supper then went rowing later.  Postal fr. Anna Monroe.
Tues. 26 Beautiful weather.  Studied Geol. Class excused for Prof. Drummond's lecture on Equatorial Africa at 11.  Took 12:50 boat for Jamestown. 1 1/2 hr. late getting back.  There at 8. or soon after.  Letter fr. Pater, Simon, Louise Langford - sent card to Anna Munroe's cousin Miss Carrie Allen.  Did not go to Quotation Match Regatta at Long Point.

Wed. 27  Postal fr. Mrs. McCoy. Wrote letters to S??? & Miss Eaton.  Postals to Mrs. McCoy& to the man at Maple Springs.  Geology in A.M. Went in P.M. with Miss Emerson to Maple Springs. I to look at the R.R. cut she to she to sit in the grove the while

title: Marion Metcalf diary [05], 1883-1889
transcription:
[?Drummund] at 9 on Nature & Religion. We found no Steamer to bring us back, so brought back a rowboat wh. belonged here at Chautauqua - were 1 1/4 hr. coming over.
Thurs. 28 Very warm - wrote to Pater & Cassius Caius - postal to Simon - Geo.. 11-12:30 - [?Drummund] at 4. Read about Niagara Falls. Rowing in evening with Miss Orgain -
Friday 29 Lovely weather. Drummond at 9 & at 2 (on Mt. Etna). At 9 on Nature & Religion, answering questions - Prof. Starr at 11. Read on "Topographic Features of Lake Shores." No letters. 
Sat. 30 Started at 5:10 A.M. for Niagara Falls with Will. Had a firstclass time & found some good specimans, crystallized minerals +c. Went to Cave of the Winds - had a picnic dinner in Prospect Park. summer at hotel. back at 12:30 - Rain while we waited at Mayville - letter from home
Sun. 31 A full, good day. Drummond at 9. saw Jorie at 11. Chaplain McCabe at 7:30 sang hyms at The Cottage until 10, after the evening service. Some good talk with Prof. Knapp. Slept some in P.M. Went to Mr. Martin's Bible Class
Mon. Aug. 1 Letter fr. Miss Howes. Postal fr. Simon. Letter fr. Solomon John. Geol. in A.M. Missionary Meeting in P.M. Rowing in evening.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [05], 1883-1889
transcription:
Tues. Aug. 2 - Letter fr. Elizabeth Eliza. Wrote to Miss Howes. Geol. in A.M. Went to Long Point for Geological purpose in P.M. Miss Emerson going with me. Heard Dr. Dickermann on Egyptian Literature at 5. Opening of Assembly in evening. Fireworks.
Wed. Aug. 3 Very warm again - Studied Geology - went on to Mayville & back on boat just before supper. Heard part of Fairbainus' lecture in A.M. Cong. Prayermeeting at 7. Miss Emerson & Mr. Waters went too - Miss Finkelstein at 8. Wrote to Solomon John.
Thurs. 4 Very warm. Went to Geol. at 11. did not stay to the class. did not go to dinner. Letter fr. Ellen Burrell. Wrote to her.
Fri. 5 Still warm but fine rain in evening. Geol. in A.M. studied in P.M. wrote to Annie. Went to bed early. Rain & wind. Miss Emerson out on lake in rain. Called on Miss Reynolds.
Sat. 6 Took 9:35 boat with Profs Starr & Gorman, Will & little John to Mayville thence train to Sherman & wagon to Gage's Gulf. Back at 6:40 P.M. a fine, cool day & a good time - found circular letter fr. E.E., K.K., Simon +c Miss Howes & letter fr. Pater. Went to Normal Class at 8 A.M. with Miss Emerson. Miss Von Finkelstein in evening. did not go out.






d time - found circular letter fr. E.E.,

title: Marion Metcalf diary [05], 1883-1889
transcription:
Sun. 7 Beautiful day. Devotional Service at 9. Dr. Adams - good. Dr. Fairbairn preached at 11. John 1:18 & 14:8.9 70 min. Cong. Went to Mr. Duncan's S.S. in afternoon - & to EvenSong at 7:30 - Sang hymns at the Cottage after it.
Mon. 8 Clear & cool. Wrote to Chemicals +c circular letter. Geol. in A.M. Heard Mrs. Lathrop in P.M. good. Lengthy conversation in evening. Mr. Reynolds, Miss Henderson +c. Went to amphitheater for a few minutes to look at Wallace Bruce -
Tues. 9 Warmer. Geol. at 10:30 - exercised early. Heard most of Dr. Fairbairn's Lecture Comparison & XIXth Cent. with IInd. Normal Class at 4. went to Miss Henderson's studio in P.M. Congregational Society at 7. Letter from Flo B. Metcalf. Card fr. Miss Eaton. wrote letter home - Miss & Mr. Reynolds called.
Wed. 10 Misty or foggy all day. Will & I took 7:25 boat to Lakewood, thence walked to Stone Ledge Quarry & back. sat under trees during quite a hard shower. reached Chaut. on 5:10 boat. very dusty walking before the shower. Congregational prayermeeting at 7. Very good. Miss Gra[?]s & Miss Rose called in evening.
Thurs. 11 Geology +c as usual. Ellen Burrell came

title: Marion Metcalf diary [05], 1883-1889
transcription:
called on Mrs Griffith & Josie, did not find them in. this afternoon took supper here with [[?]] - Procession +c of Normals in evening.
Fri. 12 Geology in A.M. Went as for as Lake - went with Miss Emerson on her way to Jamestown in P.M. Mrs. Orgain went too - went to Cong. Sociable in evening with the Schaibly's, then went rowing with Miss Henderson.
Sat. 13 Went in bathing at 8 with Mrs. Phipps & Miss Oyler. Took 9:35 boat with Will for Mayville & tramped in search of the source of the inlet of Chautauqua Lake. wandered in the woods & found nothing - back on 6:10 boat, wh. was late. Saw Mr. & Mrs. Lyon on the boat. saw Marnie Wheeler on dock at Pt. Chautauqua. Letter from Pater, [[?]]ing check.
Sun. 14 S.S. at 9. Baccalaureate Sermon by Dr. Vincent at 11. Went out no more thereafter slept some in the afternoon. had Sunday talk with Ellen Burrell & her friend. sand hymns in evening. A comfortable day as to weather.
Mon. 15 Cloudy - Geology in A.M. Cable read from Dr. Sevier at 2. Flora Crouch with some friends was there & came around to our Cottage after it. Weill & I tried again to call on Mr. & Mrs Lyon but found that they had gone home. I went with Miss

title: Marion Metcalf diary [05], 1883-1889
transcription:
Emerson to call on Mrs Duncan - Had an interesting interview with Mr. K.A. Burnell - Lent "Nonsense Songs" to Prof. Starr -
Tues. 16 Geology in A.M. Went down to Lakewood in P.M. with Mrs. Orgain - Went out Rowing with Mr. Reynolds. also to see the illumination -
Wed. 17 C.L.S.C. Recognition Day. Went to see Mrs. Orgain, Mrs. King +c - go through the golden gate - then Miss Reynolds & I started to find the source of Chautauqua Creek & Mud Creek - no success. Jollification at Muncie Cottage in evening to celebrate the 7 graduates and the 4 prizes. 
Thurs. 18 Geology in A.M. Packing +c most of the day. Dr. Jones Barker came around in P.M. just before she left for home. went to boat with her .Miss Emerson left on 6:28 train. Mr. Dunning on same train to Buffalo, with his wife & boy. Ghose Party at Amphitheater.
Fri. 19 Started for home at 6:58 A.M. Mr Waters & Mrs Orgain went to train with me - a comfortable journey - train 35 minutes late at Brocton - some late at Elyria. Prof. McKibben was on train. introduced himself & talked. married Lizzie Stillwell +is a relative of the Mussey's. Home to dinner - Nettie at station to meet me. All well.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [05], 1883-1889
transcription:
Sat. 20 Annie came on 10 oclock train & made crabapple marmalade jelly. John went to Peru +c on 5 oclock train. Mr. Root arrived in evening.
Sun. 21 Went to church, S.S. & evening meetings. rain in evening. Prof. Champlain preached in A.M. Rev. J.K. Nutting in P.M. They [drove?] over from Oberlin and stopped at our house. Theological discussion in afternoon. Sing in evening after meeting.
Mon. 22 Pickled Pears. Mr. Nutting staid until afternoon. Prof. Chamberlain & Mr. Root went at 7:03 A.M. Uncle Eliab came & arranged for family picnic. Mr. Root, summoned by telephone, came on evening train. Letter fr. Katherine -
Tues. 23 Family Picnic - E.W. & Mrs. E.W. Lucy, Edith, Carrie Soule, I.W. & Mrs. I.W. Marguerite, Will, Mayne. Mrs. I S., John, Harry, Ethel, Net, Ralph, Bunny -young I.S. - Mr. & Mrs A.S. Root. Mr. & Mrs John Leadingham, Lizzie DeWitt. Geo. Rich, wife & 2 babies. all went to Randall's & had a fine time. Lake Erie was somewhat rough. Had a geological walk - went in bathing with the Shauffler's - back about 8. Annie & husband went back to Oberlin

title: Marion Metcalf diary [05], 1883-1889
transcription:
tonight. Letter from Miss. Eaton. 
Wed. 24. Writing many Missionary Invitations - also darned stockings - In afternoon John, Ethel & I went to Oberlin with [?bu]g & Katy - went to see Annie & some of Ethel's Professors - took supper with Annie - back here about 9 -
Thurs. 25 More missionary invitations - fixed skirt & did some mending, watchpockets +c. Mrs. Helen Allbright came up in the afternoon & I went down to the post office with her. Praymeeting in evening. Mr. Ely - 
Friday. Went to Aunt Anna's in P.M. & staid (sic)
Aug. 26 to supper. Hattie Gaylord & baby Gladys are there. Nettie & John & I went to Salvation Army meeting in the evening. Read Daisy Plains.
Sat. 27 Cold. Aunt Anna's Birthday - 76 - went downtown in afternoon - & to Library in evening - brought home Donald's School Days, by Gen. O. Howard - mended & knitted.
Sun. 28 Went to church & evening meetings. Mr. Williams preached on Heaven in A.M. & on "Godliness with Contentment" in P.M.
Mon. 29 Not quite so cold, at least in middle of day. Went to dentist & had one tooth filled - Nettie & I walked up to Uncle Charles' in evening. Wallace Cathcart called.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [05], 1883-1889
transcription:
Tues. 30 Went down town in A.M. bought Jack's wedding present for Mr. Pound. In P.M. Mrs. Twiss, her Shepard & her little Gertrude came - staid to supper. Went to schoolhouse in evening, to hear Mr. Barton on "School Teaching in the Mts. of Kentucky" - Pear Honey - Mary Laundon married to Blake Johnson. Mr. Pound married.
Wed. 31 Went to ride in evening with Will, Mayne, and Lucy - Darned stockings.
Thurs. Sep. 1 Did not go to prayermeeting. On bed part of day -
Friday. 2 Missionary Tea & Thanksoffering Meeting at Chapel - Rainy in P.M. Prepared to pack -
Sat. 3 Cool. Ethel & I spent most of the day in packing. Helen Allbright, Flo M. Metcalf - & Mrs. Haines, called. Annie came at 9:35. Mr. Root, in evening - John left at 4:40. Prohibition Convention -
Sun. 4 Warmer. Went to church, S.S. & the two evening meetings - many goodby's (sic). Read "Theodora," part of it - aloud -
Mon. 5 Started at 9:28 A.M. to take express in Cleveland. Ethel & I met E.E. & Florence at Buffalo & left there at 6 - a warm day in the sleeping car but not a long one.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [05], 1883-1889
transcription:
Made acquaintance of Miss Lynch, going to Bradford Acad. Miss Davis to Abbott Acad. and the Misses Vieths to Wellesley.
Tues. 6 Saw Miss Eaton for a few minutes at Worcester at 8:30. Reached W. at 10. Did not get trunks until 4:30 or so - Box from attic came earlier. Letter from Pater in evening.
Wed. 7 Unpacking. Hung pictures in evening. Received Freshmen & friends fr. 11-1. Sat with Board of Examiners (at Lottie's request) from 3-5. Went to walk with Ethel just before supper. Tables organized for supper tonight - mine seems to be very pleasant -
Thurs. 8 College opens at 8:20. No classes today except Qual. Anal. unpacked box from Chautauqua. Letter from Louise Langford and Charlotte Halsey - went to Village - to Miss Townsend's after dinner tonight - wrote letter home
Fri. 8 Fine weather. cool evening. Phys. Geog. examinations in A.M. 3 girls - 9-11:30. Ethel & I went to walk after lunch & domestic work. I sat in parlor with Examining Board +c from 4 till 5. Helped Lottie hang her pictures this evening - Saw Bessie Leonard (Alice's sister.)

title: Marion Metcalf diary [05], 1883-1889
transcription:
Sat. Sep. 10 A damp morning, but clear later. Mr. [Orines??] was here today. I saw him for a few minutes after the Geology lecture, & walked to the station with him after lunch - 1:53 train - First Geol. lecture at 10:55. Went after gentians, but found none - Phys. Geog. examination at 4. 11 girls there. 
Sun. 11 Flower Sunday - beautiful day, cool. Dr. Edward Judson preached at 10:31, I went to church & S.S. in village. to 5 oclock meeting here. Freshman prayermeeting at 7:30, which I led. parlor crowded & time thoroughly filled. good meeting, nice girls.
Mon. 12 Cloudy or rain all day. Sent notes to Phys. Geog. girls & interviewed some. Assigned laboratory places with M. Marsh & Simon - In P.M. helped Schedule comm - In evening, some laboratory work - Letter from home - Circular Letter. Returns of Birdie Ball Morrison's children - Edith Wilkinson & Charlotte Westcott call on [?Thip] -
Tues. 13 Another gray day. Chem. classes at 9 & 1:30. Geology Lecture at 10:33. Went to walk with Simon - & in evening to [?Waban] with Carrie

title: Marion Metcalf diary [05], 1883-1889
transcription:
Soule. Worked at Lab. places +c. Letter from Pater & note from Mr. Cowan -
Wed. 14 Cloudy Still. Went to see Mrs. Manly & Mr. Manly in A.M. Made Freshmen Bible Lists. Chem. classes at 1:30 & 3:10. Meeting of Freshman Bible Teachers at 4 in #40. Praymeeting in evening.
Thus. 14 Classes at 9. 1:30 & 3:10.  Geol Lecture at 10:55. Spent 9:50 & 2:20 periods in laboratory, quizzing & being questioned. Meeting of Temperance Comm. of Christian Association at 4. Prayermeeting in evening.
Fri. 16 Simon & I went immediately after breakfast to see Elizabeth Eliza, an invalid - went late to chapel. class at 9. next period in lab. taught E.E. classes at 10 10:55 - Bible class first meeting at 2:20 - found I liked my section very much - most of remainder of afternoon I spent in the laboratory splitting wood +c. Simon & I went to the Townsend's to dinner & I to prayermeeting afterwards. Wrote letter to Mr. Cowan.
Sat. 17 Cool, beautiful weather. Geol. Lecture. Bible meeting at 11:45 with Miss Chandler & Miss Aumack. Class at 3:10. Swept rooms - Made Bible topics - studied Geology & a little chemistry - wrote to Bridie Ball Morrison -
Sun. 18 A perfect September day. warm in the middle of it. Went to church in Village. Section

title: Marion Metcalf diary [05], 1883-1889
transcription:
prayermeeting here. 17 girls present - made some progress in getting acquainted. Addie Emerson here this afternoon, also Jennie Robbins - Misses Norton, Strobridge & Sherwin called in the evening when neither of us was in - went to see Miss Jackson a few minutes.
Mon. 19 Went at 8:15 to Boston & thence to Nahaut, with Miss Roberts, Burrell, Jones, Ainsworth, Mannington, Duncan, Wetherbow, Whiegan, Moran & Ethel - a beautiful day on teh rocks & a good time. back in Boston at 3:18 - did a few errands & took 5:25 train. Receptions in evening - to Freshmen & Specials. Prof. Palmer was here & received with Miss Freeman -
Tues. 20 Letter fr. home, Mrs. Case of Akron whom we knew at Chautauqua, called yesterday when I was away. 3 classes today, as usual on Tues. Went rowing at 3:10 Faculty Meeting in evening - Lunch after it.
Wed. 21 Went to Village with Simon in A.M. stopped at the[? Dentous] and brought away loads of fruit - grapes, Porter apples, Seckel pears, Curtland pears. Did a little geological reading. Classes in P.M. Bible Comm. Meeting at #56 Stone Hall at 4. Prayer meeting & faculty meeting in evening.
Thurs. 22 Gray. cloudy. damp. class all

title: Marion Metcalf diary [05], 1883-1889
transcription:
day & laboratory toil Simon away. Letter from Jack from New York - Began home letter. Prayermeeting led by Miss Morgan. Began on chem. Note Books after prayermeeting.
Friday Sep. 23 Bible study - more Note Books. Mrs Manly & Miss Chandler came in for a few minutes after Bible class. Sent letter home - wrote to Jack. Wrote circular letter.
Sat. 24 Went to Village after chapel, & again in evening with Miss Jackson. Helped sweep & dust room - studied Geol. & did notebooks. Bks. from Sunday Library.
Sun. 25 Cool. clear, part of day. Went to church in Village - Read some in the Missionary books. Went to 5 o'clock meeting. Section meeting at Stone Hall. Prof. Moore of Andover, preached at College. Miss Howes came up to #144 in the afternoon -
Mon. 26 Foggy most of day. Note Books in A.M. Ethel & I went to ride with Grace Duncan & her two friends, in P.M. did not go to Echo Bridge - Letters from home.
Tues. 27 Classes as usual. Note Bks.
Wed. 28 Simon & I went to walk after chapel & came back by way of his house, whence we

title: Marion Metcalf diary [05], 1883-1889
transcription:
bought 2 baskets full of apples - Porters, & Pippins - only 4 gentians - classes at 1:30 & 3:10 - office hour. Dinner at Miss Whiting's table, with Lizzie Root & the 7 '80's here - went to bed at 7:30, but not at once to sleep -
Thurs. 29 Did not go to breakfast nor dinner but taught all my classes & kept my office hour, proud to say - Wrote brief letter home. Did Note Bks. of 1:30 class -
Friday 30 Foggy still, some almost sunshine - Dr. Howard Crosby lectured at 2:20 instead of Bible class. the Freshman Bible teachers had their meeting in #144 at 3:10. Wrote to Uncle George, & to renew subscription to Independent. Letter from Annie Reynold's.
Sat. Oct. 1 Still foggy & gray. Classes as usual - went to Village in the rain after lunch. Swept after dinner. Went to Miss Hill's room at 7 to talk about gymnasium work for this winter. Did Note Books thereafter.
Sun. 2 Some rain - clear in evening - Communion Sunday at College - Dr. Washington Gladden preached in A.M. Missionary Meeting in evening. Dr. Ba[?] of Harport. Read some in "Heroines of the Mission Field" -

title: Marion Metcalf diary [05], 1883-1889
transcription:
Mon. 3 Wrote to Wilder, Harl, Annie Reynolds, Uncle George - Letters from John, Wilder, Pater, Mrs. Solomon John - card of little William Duffies Van Pelt - went to village with Simon in the rain in P.M. Memorial Service - Mr. Durant in evening - Miss Freeman gave the address -
Tues. 4 Classes as usual - Faculty Meeting in evening. We went chestnutting in Wellesley Hills with aid of the Whiting boys in P.M.
Wed. 4 Classes in P.M. Studying up Laws of Boyle, Charles +c - Prayermeeting in evening. Miss Chapin led - called on Miss M.R. Roberts.
Thurs. 5 Classes all day - & office hour - did not get outdoors at all - Prayermeeting led by Miss Tuttle. Lovely weather - 
Fri. 6 Fine weather - Notebooks & papers - Bible class - Edith here with their artist friends from 3 till 7:13. Miss Plaisted - #6 Beacon St. 
Sat. 7 Fine weather. Classes as usual. Sunday Library - Minnie Hall here with a friend. I was with them from about 1:20-2:20 Mrs. Emerson of Rockford was here. Went to Village with Miss Jackson after dinner - 
Sun. 8 cloudy, except early in morning - Dr. Miller of Philadelphia, preached at College

title: Marion Metcalf diary [05], 1883-1889
transcription:
Went to church + Sunday School in Village-
Slept in afternoon. Prayermeeting led
by Grace Eastman-
Mon. 10 Went to Boston at 7:54. heard Dr. Joseph
Parker at Tremont Temple at 12. Called on
Mrs. Watson on Ashburton Place. came out at
12:15 Concert in evening. did not go much.
Sent letter home.
Tues 11 Classes as usual. Chem. Dept. +
sister with Mary Ainsworth. Went on 3:39
train to Boston. Went to the Fair, + came
out at 9. Had a good time.
Wed. 12 Sat for pictures at Pach's in A.M.
kept office hour. Classes at 1:30 + 3:10-
prayermeeting in evening. Miss Freeman led.
Thurs. 13 Classes. Com. Meeting at 4. Office
hour at 4:30- Went out doors at noon.
Prof. Drummond spoke in evening, and
after it, Lottie, Katherine, + I went to see
Miss Vida Scudder in Ellen's rooms had
quite an interesting time.
Wrote to Mrs. Ballington Booth.
Fri. 13 Prof Drummond spoke this afternoon
in Bible hour - in the evening Helen Bald-
-win + I went to prayermeeting in the Village
Sat. 15 Fine weather. Prof Miles had the
toothache, so did not stay to take a walk

title: Marion Metcalf diary [05], 1883-1889
transcription:
