Fri. 18 Wrote brief letter to Pater. Invitation to next Reception sent to Prof. & Mrs. Drown, Mrs. Watson and Mr. Safford. Valentines at table. Helen Baldwin was at our table and dinner and we had much fun with the Valentines.
Sat. 19 Taught Mineralogy class about use of blowpipe +c -  gave directions for first blowpipe work - Marion Marsh & I took dinner at Swipson Cottage - Katherine was there also & Edith Wilkinson - mended hose in evening -
Sun. 20 Went to church, S.S. & Young People's Meeting in Village - taught Mrs. Danas class. Miss Jackson went with me in evening - Dr. Clark preached at College - Memorial Service for Mr. Durant in evening - very many away for Sunday & Washington's Birthday.
Mon. 21 Letters from Pater & Mayo - Tore black cashmere dresss & spent a long time mending it - read over Mr. Boffin +c

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
spent the whole afternoon rehearsing Mr. Boffin +c at Waban Cottage - Reception at Dana Hill - not invited -
Tues. 22 Washington's Birthday. Holiday - wrote long letters home & to Solomon John. began one to Marion Sheldon - Rehearsal at Waban all the afternoon - Dickens Party in evening - good fun & scalloped oysters - left there about 10:30 -
Wed. 23 Retired fr. public life about 11 oclock A.M. E.E. taught my 1:30 class - Read Tom Brown at Rugby - Returned borrowed garments in A.M. including Mr. Mauly's coat +c -
Thurs. 24 Did not go to breakfast or dinner, but taught my three classes -
Friday 25 Classes as usual. Worked at Quant. Anal. most of day. Bible lesson at 2:20 in No. 102.
Sat. 26 Letter from Pater & the [[?muther]] in A.M. & another in P.M> - Went to Boston at 11:07 - found that Dr. Morton did not have

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
the 10-1 office hour on Saturday - Bought some books - went to Dr. Mendiths' Bible Class - came out at 5. Birthday party for Alice Dixon in Chem. Lect. Room this evening - Went to see Miss Emerson & talk over Chautauqua a few minutes.
Sun. 27 Clear, bright weather - very slushy walking - went to church & S.S. in Village. Mrs. Dana was there & taught her own class. I went into Mr. Cowan's - Did not go out in evening - Read some in Jerry McAuley -
Mon. 28 Did Mineralogy experiments in A.M. Mended hose. Reception in P.M. Mrs. Watson came. met Mr. & Mrs. Bird of Auburndale. he a cousin of MIss Dascomb. also Mr. Tunier an Oberlin graduate now in Andover Theol. Sem. Pupil's Concert in evening - went not, but tried to fix my red gown.
Mar. 1 Classes as usual - Faculty meeting in evening - decided to seat Beethoven

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
Society on platform for remainder of year and to postpone Spring Vacation one week to include Fast Day, Good Friday & Easter Sunday
Wed. 2 Began letter home - Gave Miss Condit a Written Lesson in Quant. Anal. Led teachers' prayermeeting in evening - Episcopal Service at 4. did not go - went to walk with Simon, down to Mrs. Manley's -
Thurs. 3 Mineralogy class omitted. Went to Dana Hall after dinner to return the Guyot's Phys. Geog - & was too late back for prayermeeting - Wrote home & to Uncle George - M. Marsh in bed.
Fri. 4 Class at 9. Quant class omitted - went to Boston at 11 to see Dr. Morton - do a little shoppping then to Mrs. Munhall's Bible Reading at Clarendon St. Church. came out at 5 - late to dinner - Gen. Crook & Mr. & Mrs. Tibbles were at the College & spoke in Bible hour. I should have been invited to lunch with them

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
if I had been here. Letter to Ethel -
Sat. 5 Class at 10:55. Dusted room - mended stockings - took exercise - did Note Book +c - Simon went home for Sunday. Prof. Palmer read fr. the Odyssey in evening -
Sun. 6 Snow, Hail, Rain - went to church & S.S. in Village. Mrs. Dana taught her class - Went home to dinner with Mrs. Cowan & had a very nice time. Pres. Ward spoke at 5 at College - & Mr. Cooper of Baldwin Place Home for Little Wanderers, at 7:30 -
Mon. 7 Went to Boston at 8:14 with Miss Howes. tried vainly to get tickets for Jas R. Lowell's Lectures - bought dress for Annie & one fore myself. Went to Dr. Munhall's Bible Reading, introductory to the service on sanctification. Came out at 5 - Mr Dickinson lectured in the evening - went not -

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
Tues. 8 Rushed all day. Mineralogy & Gen Chem. & preparations for quantitative distillation of K2Cr2O2 with HCl - Head Meeting in evening - 6:30-9:30 - 
Wed. 9 Another very busy day. Quantitative business. Prayermeeting led by Miss Case - Letter from Ethel -
 Thurs. 10 Snow, rain, hail, blow. Mineralogy omitted. Prayermeeting by Miss Andrews. Prof. Bournegane 6:30 the first of his course of lectures on Theisus - Letter home. [note in margin: Miss Freeman went home.]
Fri. 11 Clear & rather cold. Class at 9. Did a little Mineralogy work - & some Quant. Anal. distillation of MnO2 with HCl. Went to Boston at 12:15 - to buy handkerchiefs & stockings - & try to exchange my dress & was unsuccessful in the latter - went to Dr. Munhall's last Bible Reading on sanctification - Came out at 5 & went to teat at Miss Townsend's with Simon - had a good time there - very cold & windy evening -

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
Sat. 12 Very muddy weather. Mineralogy Class at 10:55. Went to Millbury on 2:16 train, Miss Fuller's friend, Miss Hazen, to occupy my room over Sunday. Found the Millbury  people all well.
Sun. 13 Went to church & S.S. & to Union Temperance Meeting in evening where I heard Gen. John L. Swift. was somewhat disappointed in him - 
Mon. 14 Left Millbury at 9:50 - made a very brief call on Mrs. Thayer first - reached Wellesley at 11:07 & found 2 letters from home. Worked at Mineralogy - +c - 
Tues. 15 Classes as usual. Quantitative work - No Faculty meeting.
Wed. 16 Wrote letter home - Quantitative work - Rev. Carlton P. Mills conducted services here at 4 & his wife, Helen Briggs, came with him - they could not stay to dinner. We '80's went to Miss Whiting's table however. Ellen Burrell led prayer meeting - went to Miss Eaton & Lottie -

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
Thurs. 17 Examination at 11:30 - did papers until nearly 11:30 P.M. Went to walk with Simon. Kate Kelsey led the prayermeeting on Christian conservation -
Fri. 18 Examination at 9. Went to Boston at 12:15. did a little shopping & went to Dr. Munshall's service. it was the best Praise Meeting I ever attended. A business meeting of '80 in the evening -
Sat. 19 Mineralogy labor. Chemistry Note Books. gave Min. class a written lesson. Did not go to Lowell's lecture - nobody went on the ticket. Celebrated Marie Wheeler's birthday at table - with diced beef cooked in milk & presents piled high -
Sun. 20 Retired to private life soon after breakfast - Prog. Townsend of Boston University preached. Read Independents & Christian Unions & some in the Bible -
Mon. 21 Did not get up to breakfast. But rose soon after & did Note Books diligentlay all morning - went to Boston at 1:53

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
to Dr. Munshall's Bible Reading on The Devil - came out at 5 - Finished the Note Books in the evening - Letter from Pater.
Tues 22 Classes as usual. Simon & I went to village in evening to hear Mrs. Livermore on Women in the War -
Wed. 23 Mineralogy Work. Went in A.M. to S.S. Conversation in Village for about an hour. heard Mr. Peloubet teach the Review Lesson. it was a grand lesson. Oxygen experiments at 1:30 - Prayermeeting led by MIss Tuttle -
Thurs. 24 Classes as usual. Went at 3:39 to Newtonville to see Lilla D. Patterson & very unexpectedly stayed all night - had a fine time -
Fri. 25 Came back fr. Newtonville on 8:29 train. A.M. - fine morning - walked up fr. station - Sent letter home - Studied Quant - Class met at 3:10. Faculty Meeting to elect a delegate to Columbia College Celebration -

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
Went to Alma A{?umeck's] room in evening to assist in disposing of a box of candy +c -
Sat. 26 Went down to Mrs. Manley's with Miss Howes in A.M. Dusted room. Mended 3 dresses. Mrs. Fuller came up and cut Florence Marsh's hair. in Chem. Store Room. Simon went away to spend Sunday -
Sun. 27 A cool, spring like day - went to church in A.M. & Young Peoples Meeting in P.M. Dr. Duryea was expected to preach at Coll - but could not, as his wife is very ill.
Mon. 28 Clouds and rain. Mended clothes. Wrote to Kitty and Russell. Anna Stockbridge Tuttle, Caro Bowman Parkinson, Nellie Brown Giles, Helen Briggs Mlle. Birdie Ball Morrison about Tree day and baby pictures. Went to Boston at 1:53 to Mr. Munhall's Bible Reading & back at 5. The Beethoven Society gave the Cantata of King Reve's daughter this evening - very good indeed, but bad air in chapel. Charlotte Westcott came to see me - no letters. "The Open Court" came -

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
Tues. 29 3 classes. Wrote to Anna Stockbridge Tuttle, Carrie Wheeler Cooper, Addie Emerson Thompson, Lizzie McCleery Davis - finishing my 9 class letters. Letter from Pater & one from Helen Kitchell asking for some rock sections - Meeting of Board of Examiners at 6:30
Wed. 30 Cold. 10 degrees below zero in morning - High wind - March going out like a lion - Term closed at 12:30 - Did Note books - looked up sections to send to Helen Kitchell - wrote letter home - went to Village twice -
Thurs. 31 Beautiful, clear cool weather - went to Boston at 10 - to Dr. Morton - to do some shopping - & to Dr. Munchell's Bible Reading - came out at 5 - Simon was on same train, to return some books to the Wellesley Library - he came up to supper with me. then I went home with him & staid [sic] all night - Had a fine time -
Friday Apr 1 Came up from Wellesley Hills at 8:29. Postal fr. Elizabeth Eliza -

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
Began work on Minerals Room. I did about 3 hurs. work in A.A> Went to Boston at 1:53, to Dr. Munchall's last Bible Reading - came out at 5 - Mdlle. See had friend to tea. Prof. Kohn (?) & his fiancee - + a Parisian. Mr. Augell - Went to prayermeeting in Village with Miss Southworth -
Sat. 2 Snowstorm & high wind all day - worst storm of whole winter, perhaps Plumber +e at work in #153 all day - I put in 6 hrs. work on the minerals - mended hose & fooled a little with Miss Jackson & Mrs. McCoy in evening - Long letter from Solomon John -
Sun. 3 A bright, beautiful day. walking of course rather bad. Went to church, S.S. & the two evening meetings - Miss Southworth met with me in the evening. Read more in Ephesians.
MOn. 4 Another bright day. Read a little before breakfast. Put in a good 6 hours of work. Went to call on the Baldwins - found only Helen at home. Read with Miss Jackson in evening. MIss Southworth came in to see

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
me. Letter from Mr. Root. Wrote to Mr. Root and to Uncle George. Finished the minerals in 3 cases in Room 0.
Tues. 5 Gray in A.M. but clear in P.M. Spent sometime mending dress, so put in only 5 1/2 hrs' work today. Led prayers. Worked in Room 0 in A.M. and with blowpipe in P.M. Read "Hoosier Schoolmaster" to Miss Jackson and Mrs. Nary in evening - Sent letter to Simon -
Wed. 6 A lovely day - somewhat cooler - Six good hours of blowpipe work. Postal card from Uncle George - wrote one to him. Finished Hoosier Schoolmaster.
Thurs. 7 Last day in Massachusetts. Beautiful cold weather. 4 1/2 hrs. work. in A.M. at blowpiping - in P.M. looking over Mineralogy Cases at 5th floor Centre - Mr. Root came about 3:15 and stayed until 7:13. Walked to station with him - went to bed soon after 8 o'clock.
Fri. 8 Good Friday - Clear and cold. Full moon. Put in 7 1/2 hrs' work, mostly at blowpiping. a little Quantitative study

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
in evening. Maud Williamson & I went to prayermeeting in the Village. Miss Jackson and Miss Howes went to Boston this afternoon. Short letter from Pater. Hair done 32 blowpipe minerals this vacation.
Sat. 9 Worked a little on Quant. Anal. & Gen. Chem. for first lessons next term & not more than 1 1/2 hrs. good solid work - Went to Boston at 12:15. to do a little shopping and do to Dr. Merdith's Bible Class - met Miss Howes there - came out at 5:25. Read "Cecil Dreeine" to Miss Jackson & Miss Harding in evening & sewed new braid on to black cashmere dress - One of the Laundry girls died here today -
Sun. 10 Easter Sunday - very warm summer day - went to church S.S., and evening meetings.
Mon. 11 Wrote to Pater, Annie, John, Harl, Ethel, & Harry. Letter from Mr. Dana. wrote to him also, about analysis of fertilizer. Did a little blowpiping in P.M. Had room swept - started at 4:28 for Millbury

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
Mr. & Mrs. Water came up to Uncle Georg's in evening.
Tues. 12 Cooler & cloudy part of day. Went to village with Harry - also had quite a tramp with him, to top of a hill near by. Uncle George went to Association at Douglas. Early to bed. [note in margin: Dress fitted.]
Wed. 13 Cool. Had quite a long ride with Uncle George in A.M. Velvet waist fitted in P.M. Went down to Mrs. Water & unexpectedly staid [sic] to tea. Prayermeeting in evening.
Thurs. 14 Breakfast at 6. Reached Wellesley at 8:15 A.M. Classes at 9:00 10:55 & 1:30. Ozone experiments - Went in P.M. to make a last call on the Baldwins. Prayermeeting led by Miss Hayes - started hymns - 
Fri. 15 Class at 9:00 & thereafter retired to private life - Found her on return letters from Caro B. Parkinson, Carrie Wheeler Cooper, Helen Kitchell, Mr. Dana - Henry Holt & Co. - letter came yesterday from Miss Eaton - this morning fr. Pater. Tonight

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
from the Muther. Jack & Ethel sent letters today to Henry Holt & Co. & Miss Eaton. Jo Cass here this afternoon & over night -
Sat. 16 Letter from Kitty Eno Russell with Eugenie's picture. Postal from Uncle George. umbrella safe. Did not go to breakfast but went to lunch & dinner. Analysed 4 minerals & began to study up for Mr. Dana's fertilizers - wh. arrived tonight.
Sun. 17 Cool & clear. Did not go to Village in A.M. but went to the Young People's Meeting on evening, then to  Missionary Meeting here whereat spoke Dr. J.L. Phillips of the Sautol Mission in India. Bishop Andres (Meth.) preached in A.M.
Mon. 18 Snowstorm & wind - Letter from Pater in A.M. letter fr. Helen Briggs Mills, with picture of little Margaret, in P.M. Worked on the Fertilizers nearly all day - finished the NaN03 - stated the NH3 test - & standardized Ur solution for phosphate test - Went through Registry with E.E. - or Simon to make list of girls who can be recommended to teach Chem -

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
Min. or Geol. Had a talk with Edith Harris about Salvation Army - Simon & I went out for a little walk in evening.
Tues. 19 Classes as usual. Worked on the fertilizers all the time wh. could be spared from classes. Head Meeting & Faculty Meeting in evening - lunch after it -
Wed. 20 Letters fr. Ralph & Mayo - Wrote letter home - class at 1:30. Worked on the fertilizers most of day - Prayermeeting in evening. Went to bed early -
Thurs. 21 Classes. Fertilizers - finished, except the NH3 test & sent report to Mr. Dana - went to walk with Miss Howes & Miss Kelsey. Prayermeeting led by Miss Montague - Read Salvation Army Book - rules for Field officers
Friday 22 Warm bright day. Class at 9. Quiz on oxygen. Worked on Minerals, Grape Sugar - NH3 test in the bones, +c - sent report to Mr. Dana - went to walk with Miss Howes in afternoon - to village with Simon in evening -

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
Sat. 23 Cloudy day - a little rain in evening - Quant. work & Mineralogy work. Went to Boston at 5 with the Townsend's to Salvation Army meeting - welcome to Marshall Ballington Booth & wife - came out at 11:15 & went home with the Townsend's for the night -
Sun. 24 Warm, bright day - went to church with Miss Townsend. (Lobster salad for breakfast) - did not stay to S.S. - went to 5 oclock meeting at College & Young People's Meeting in Village - 
Mar. 25 Letter from Mr. Dana enclosing $5 - came Saturday night - also letter from Pater - Went to Boston at 12:15 - with Mr. & Mrs. Manly, Miss Stratton & Miss Howes to hear Mrs. Ballington Booth on Humanity & its Causes - very fine indeed - I went also to the Banquet at teh Argyle Rink, where I waited on table - came out at 9. Saw Lilla D. Patterson & her husband at the Tremont Temple meeting in afternoon. [note in margin: Concert by Dr. Maas -]
Tues. 26 A little snowstorm & some rain - clear & bright in P.M.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
classes as usual. Head Meeting from 6:30 to 10 P.M. Did not go outdoors today.
Wed. 27 Fine weather again. Work on Sugar and Silver, CO2 experiments in 1:30 class. Prayermeeting led by Miss Emerson. Prof. Loisette is to give his Mercury lessons here soon. Went to bed early.
Thurs. 28 Rose at 5. Wrote letter home and one to Uncle George, before breakfast. Letter from Uncle Geo. telling of the severe illness of his wife & death of the baby. Helen Cooper's picture arrived. Quant. work. Christian Association meeting in P.M. Early to bed. [Note in margin: Letter from Lilla D. Patterson]
Fri. 29 Wrote to Carrie Wheeler Cooper and to Lilla D. Patterson before breakfast. Class at 9. Quant. work mostly for remainder of day - Meeting of Board of Examiners from 6:15 till about 9. Board of Visitors here  today, but we [underlined] sawnothing of them. Quant. class met at 3:10. Dr. Scudder from Chicago, going to Japan, spoke in chapel at Bible hour. Rain -

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
Sat. 30 Alternate sunshine and rain Went to Millbury at 7:28. Uncle Geo. was at station - tried on dress & brought it away with me. rode to Worcester with Uncle Geo. & Harry & took 4 o'clock train here, arriving at 5:05. Went to Mdlle. See's little party in evening & told Miss Freeman about Mrs. Booth. Brief letter from Ammie who was married today. I suppose. 
Sun. May 1 A beautiful May day. warm & bright. Went to ch. & S.S. in Village taught Mrs. Dana's class. Went to walk with Florence Marsh in afternoon. Missionary meeting in evening. Rev. Mr. Brown of Harpoot, who also preached here today -
Mon. May 2 Another fine day - Interview with Miss Freeman in A.M. also some work on minerals. Went to Cambridge on 1:53 train - & had a pleasant afternoon with Miss Eaton, supper wtih her in Newton. Back at 7:13 - Temperance Lecture by Mr. Yeames - good - spoke of National Temp. Hospital in London, where not even alcoholic tinctures are used - Life Insurance Company, number

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
of deaths anticipated in Total Abstinence section never realized - in moderate drinking section, always exceeded. 1526 women arrested for drunkenness in streets of Boston. Apr. to Sept. 1884. Population increased 32% 1870 - 1880 - consumption of liquors, 73% - letter from Uncle Herbert about Abbie's coming here Sept. '88. More stuff from Mrs. Dana with a note - P.P.C. cards fr. Mrs. Watson & Mr. Safford - Sent invitations to four couples for the next Reception.
Tues. 3 Classes as usual. Began Carbon in Gen. Chem. Worked some on Mr. Dana's samples. Letter fr. Pater, the Mither, Harl & Ejith. Council Meeting & Gen. Faculty Meeting in evening. 
Wed. 4 Very warm. Worked on fertilizers in A.M. & P.M. Had a gentleman in the 1:30 class from some Normal School.  Flau[[?]] experiments. Wrote letter home. Went to prayer meeting, led by Miss L.F. Clark.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
Thurs. 5 Postal from Lille - worked on the fertilizers. Began Illuminating Gas in 1:30 class. Wrote to Mrs. Booth, Prof. Turner of Lincoln, Ill. Prof. Starr of Cor[[?]] College. & Mrs. Durant - Prayermeeting - Miss Barrows -
Friday. 6 Class at 8. Spent remainder of dat, for the most part, on Bones & such.
Sat. 7 Took 10 o'clock train for Boston - thence to Andover to spend Sunday with Lilla D. Patterson - reached there about 1 o'clock. Had a good social time - open fire in evening. Mrs. Beard came in -
Sun. 8 Beautiful day - very warm in afternoon. Went to the chapel church & heard Prof. Egbert Smyth morning and afternoon - Met Prof. Churchill, who was very friendly & introduced me to Prof. Smyth - went in afternoon, after church, to see Belle French, Miss McKeen, Mrs. Mead, Mrs.  Anderson (Clara Potter). Malcolm Ely & George

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
Worthington came to call - staid [sic] at long time - by the open fire & we so enjoyed it - Mr. Beard came in again after they left.
Mon. 9 Warm, fine weather. Left Andover at 9:47 & Boston at 11:05 reached Wellesley at 11:44. Found letter from Lottie, paper from Wi. & letter fr. Mrs. Seymour - Letter from Pater arrived tonight - Reception this afternoon - Dr. Drown & his wife were there - we had a fine time with them. Dr. Judson Smith & wife were there, also Dr. Clark, Dr. Alden & Dr. Webb.
Tues. 10 Letter from Annie. Wrote letter home. Classes as usual & Head Meeting 6:30 - 9:45 (including lunch - Took a nap in afternoon - 
Wed. 11 Letter fr. the mither - wrote to Annie, Lottie Roberts & Mayo. Queen Kapiolani +c came to the Coll. at 10 - left on 12:15 train - we had some short speeches & singing in chapel. procession &

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
tree planing - 9:50 - 10:55 classes were omitted. Went rowing in evening. the Townsends, E.E., Simon & I - Miss Williston was with us until time for 7:13 train - Letter fr. & about Woman's Tribune of Beatrice, Neb.
Thus. 12 Letter fr. Prof. Starr, the Chautauqua Mineralogy & Geology man - "Analysis of Commercial Fertilizers" from Prof. Drown. Examination at 1:30 - took about a dozen of that class through the College gasworks at 4 - Prof. Loisette gave the firsit Mercury Lesson this evening - Marid Stowe came to see me about her work for next year.
Fri. 13 Dr. Edward Beecher of Andover lectured in Bible hour, on Samual & the Prophetic Order. We went to Miss Townsend's to tea. Simon, Elizabeth Eliza & I. I came back early & went to bed - Exam at 9.
Sat. 14 Did not go to breakfast - but did to dinner. Worked at Examination papers.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
Sun. 15 Went to church in Village. Rev. D. J. Hill preached at College - Dr. Beecher talked to the Sophomores in teh evening. 
Mon. 16 Wrote to Miss Eaton & to A. Lowell & Co. Publishers. Letter fr. Prof Turner, the Martha Vineyard Geology man - We '80's except Ilene Burnell, went to Newton Heighlands to lunch with Helen Briggs - Nellie Brown Giles was here - Mr. Mills was not there. Went at 12. back at  5. Reading Sheridan's Rivals by Mr. Leland Powers, in evening - great fun
Tues. 17 Classes as usual. Faculty meeting evening - Wrote to Edith - 
Wed. 18 Worked on Mineralogy equations - Prof. Loisette's second lecture occupied the evening from 7 - 9:20. Letter from Jack. 
Thurs. 19 H2S experiments at 1:30 - Mineralogy class. Equations - at 10:55 - Marion Marsh led the prayer meeting at 7:30.
Friday 20 Directors of Am. Classical Schools at Athens, held their Annual Meeting here today. Heads of Departments took

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
dinner with them at Norumbega - I went - meeting to arrange schedule of examinations - at Norumbega at 8 or soon after. Quant. class met at 3:00 for lesson on Water Anlaysis - wrote letter home. 
Sat. 21 Mineralogy class at 10:55 - on Equations. Went to the Fair at Miss Williston's House in Auburndale in the afternoon. and to the Missionary Entertainment in Gymnasium here in the evening - Swept room late in evening - [note in margin: Went to Miss Eaton and to Pensy Richards]
Sun. 22 A good day - Mr Moody preached morning & evening - A.M. on The Holy Spirit of Power for Service - evening - "What seek ye" "Seek ye the Lord while He may be found" - "Seek ye first the Kingdom of God & His Righteousness." There was an after meeting which was very good & beautiful. I went to it with Grace Van Eps. 
Mon. 23 Still no rain - warm but a good breeze - went to Boston at 7:54 - did shopping & came out at 11. Am. Hist. Ass. & Am.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
Economic Ass. - were received here this afteroon & among them came John Martin Vincent of Elyria Ohio - Pupil's Concert this evening - Letter form Miss Eaton & one from Pater - sent letter to Malcolm Ely -
Tues. 24 Warm weather still & no rain - Classes as usual - First lesson in Recognition of Hard Specimens in Mineralogy at 10:55. Meeting of Acad. Council in evening. Letter from Persey Richards wh. I answered at once o nearly so -
Wed. 25 Prof. Loisette's last lecture - not so long as the second and more to the point. Wild flowers sent to Framingham prison yesterday - Went to walk with Mabel Stockbridge after dinner - Somewhat showing - 
Thurs. 26 Classes as usual in A.M. John Vincent came in the afternoon - we went over to Hunneurwell's he staid [sic] to driver & then after called on Mrs. Manly & saw Miss Stratton - Annual Meeting of

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
Christian Association in evening - election of officers -
Friday 27 Tree Day - showery - Carrie Soule & I went at 5:20 A.M. in rubber boots & long dresses, after violets to put on Annie Montague's tress. We had to change all our clothes when we came back, & were not late to breakfast. Hattie Blake, Minnie Hall, Annie Colby, Hattie Pierce & Helen W. N[[?]]erosa came to Tree Day. also Ada Ayer, of course, Katherine had a bad cold & could not go out, but we all took dinner with her at Stone Hall - & were "recepted" at Dana Hall in the evening -
Sat. 28 Letters from Cassius Caius, Annie & Persy Richards - sent letter home - Mineralogy class at 10:55. Brushed & dusted room. Made Annual Report of Chem. Dept. for Board of Trustees - Microscopic Society celebrated its 10th anniversary by an exhibition this evening. Rev. Robt. Humes was here. Mr. H.W. Mabie

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
spend Sunday here - Rainy & cold
Sunday May 29 Still cold & rainy - Dr. Pratt of Hartford Theol. Sem. preached today - his wife is here with him - went to church in Village. Mr. Cowan preached on "I have fought the good fight" - Simon is away for Sunday.
Monday 30 Decoration Day - looked cloudy, but did not rain. Note from Malcolm Ely - also from Persy Richards, who did not come today with the S.A. captains, as I had expected. Wrote to Jack & Ethel. Looked over Mineralogy Note Books - went to R.R. station twice. Lecture by Mr. Mabie
Tues. 31 3 classes as usual. began on Silicates in Mineralogy. Council Meeting in evening. Rainy day. Wrote to Wilder.
Wed. June 1 Rainy, damp - cold. Letter from Pater. Dr. Abbott talked to us at the Teachers' prayer meeting on City Evangelization. Wrote to Wilder & Lottie Roberts.
Thurs. 2 Warmer. Chem. examination at 1:30 did papers in evening. Mr. Manly led the

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
prayer meeting. Wrote to Persy Richards.
Friday 3. Chemistry examination at 9:00. Did papers. & made up averages. Simon gave me a shampooing. Sent a "sassy" letter to Pater - Junior Promenade Day - showery - grounds beautifully illuminated.
Sat. 4 Last Mineralogy lesson at 10:55. The Phillips Academy boys did not come this afternoon nor did I hear from them. Float came off this evening in very cool weather.
Sun. 5 Elizabeth Slater had her sister at our table today. Florence Soule's cousin was there at dinner. Went to church in the village & heard a very good sermon fr. Prof Ropes, of Bangor Theol. Sem., Nellie Ladd's brother in law. Dr. Pentice preached at College - Short Vesper Service after prayers in evening -
Mon. 6 Went to 10:50 train & found nobody for me. Went to 11:50 train & found the two Misses Richards - they were here until 5. We went to Hunnerwell's in

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
the afternoon, Miss Howes with us - Concert in evening, but Mr & Mrs C.N. Allen +c. Seniors to Plymouth today on Ex. Gov. Claflin's invitation -
Tues. 7 Classes at 9. & 1:30 - N1NH3 & HNO3 experiments - nearly knocked myself down with NH3 in A.M.& with NO2 in P.M. Faculty Meeting in evening - also Council Meeting - letter from home. Wrote to Prof. Starr & to Miss Eaton.
Wed. 8 Finished looking over all the Bunsen burners in the Dept. Phosphrus [sic] at 1:30. Simon & I overhauled the Catalogue Chemical Cupboard - went to Miss Townsend's after dinner - then to prayer meeting led by Dr. Speakman - Saw Mrs. Case about Domestic Workers for next year. Simon had company - Letter from Wilder - & one fr. Lilla D. Patterson
Thurs. 9 Taught class at 9. & was on bed for remainder of day. Read Vanity Fair - The Townsends were up in the evening - Letter from Birdie Ball Morrison -

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
Friday June 10 Examinations began today - Did not go to breakfast & spent most of A.M. preparing for Mineralogy examination, wh. was administered in afternoon. Did not go to dinner -
Sat. 11 Went to Boston at 10 - to see Munkacsy's "Christ before Pilate" - & go to Dr. Merdith's last Bible Class - came out at 5:25. took lunch with the Townsend's at Macdonald's - Did Mineralogy papers in evening. Shakesper Soc. had an open meeting this evening - Letter fr. Ethel - & one from Louella Smith -
Sun. 12 Lovely weather, as yesterday - went to church, Sunday School & two evening meetings in Village - Rev. Geo Burell preached morning & evening - Went to 5 o'clock prayermeeting, led by Bertha Bailey - Discussed matters in general in No. 103.
Mon. 13 Graduates' Concert this evening - Misses Smeallie, Hand, Howe, Noyes, Goodwin. Wrote to Anna Rich-

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
Tues. 14 Academic Council Meeting 6:30-10:30 - Made up averages +c.
Wed. 15 General Faculty meeting 7:30-11:30 - discussed Regulations -
Went rowing with Townsends - 6-7:30
Thurs. 16 Went to Boston at 8 - to buy Annie Rich's wedding present - & a chirometer - came out at 11:05. Tried to go to Miss Currier's (Newton) this evening - but went not - Prayermeeting led by Miss Case -
Fri. 17 Recorded marks +c - Head Meeting 6:30-10:45.
Sat. 18 Made out & sent Cards of passed examination to all the Chem. Dept - with help of E.E. & domestic worders. E.E. & I worked on Chem. Library - Went to call on the Eastmans - took tea at the Townsends - delicious strawberry shortcake - Alumnae coming back
Sun. 19 Baccalaureate Sunday - went to ch. & S.S. in village in A.M. Service here at 4 P.M. - Rev. Frederic Courtney -

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
Evening prayers & Vespers Service at 7:30. May Sleeper here -
Mon. 20 Worked and planned at Dining Room Comm. business - Presentation of Statue of Elaine in P.M. Concert in evening, to wh. I scarcely went - wrote letter home -
Tues. 21 Commencement Day - cloudy - almost showery - everything went off well, including Dining Room arrangements - Carrie Wheeler Cooper & husband, Lilla D. Patterson & husband & mother, Hattie Pierce, Ada Ayer, and our College '80's sat together at dinner. Reception in evening - quite late to bed -
Wed. 22 Alumnae Day. After dinner speeches by Miss Hurll, Lathrop-Ayer, Carrie Wheeler-Cooper, Lilla D. Patterson - had a call from Miss Fannie Herrick and a friend this evening - Packed in evening - showery.
Thurs. 23 Finished packing - Looked over certificates from 9 till 12:30 or so - Rain.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
Took 1:53 train to Boston & 6:00 train to Fall River boat - with Miss Howes.
Fri. 24 All day on the Hudson - warm & bright - Had supper in Albany - & took train at 10:40 P.M.
Sat. 25 Reached home at noon. Nettie at station. Miss Howes went home with me till 5 o'clock train. Annie was here. Jack & ethel came from Oberlin at 1:30 - all went back tonight.
Sun. 26 Did not go to church - Mr. Williams exchanged with Mr. Williamson today - went to Young Peoples Meeting & evening service - Read to children in afternoon -
Mon. 27 At home all day. Edith & Lucy came over in the afternoon - Mrs. Leonard called. Wrote to Miss Neely. did some mending -
Tues. 28 - Nettie & the mither went to Oberlin this morning - Nettie stayed with Annie - wrote to Miss Jackson.
Wed. 29. I went to Oberlin at 7:00 & came

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
back at 10. Warm weather - went to hear St. John on Fair Ground in afternoon - like him well.
Thurs. 30 Nettie came home at 10 - Ethel & Hal at 1 - Harl in evening - went to hear Sobieski in A.M. Prayermeeting in evening -
Fri. July 1. S.S. Picnic - at Vermilion - Shadduck's Grove - 10 of us went - had a good time - a very warm day - Harl & I went over to the Temperance Camp in evening & heard the Silver Lake Quartette.
Sat. 2 Drove to Oberlin with Hall & Kate, after his things & Ethel's & John's - went to see Annie Root & Annie Leadingham - had dinner with Annie at Mrs. Blaine's - reached home about 7 P.M. Very warm.
Sun. 3 Very warm, not to say hot. Went to church, S.S. & 2 meetings in evening. Mr. Williams preached in A.M. on work of Am. Cong. Union. Mr. Wilbur in P.M. on "Bear ye one another's burdens, & so fullfill the law of Christ." read to

title: Marion Metcalf diary [04], 1883-1889
transcription:
children in P.M.
Mon. 4 Still very warm. a quiet Fourth - Rain in evening. John came home.
Tues. 5 A little cooler, but not much, on bed most of morning. Went downtown in afternoon - to select a set of dishes for Annie - take shoes & watch to be repaired - & had (manilla) to be trimmed. In evening went down to Aunt Anna's - stopped at Jennie Hall's on way home - spent the night with Helen Twiss Allbright -
Wed. 6 Annie came on - in the morning & her husband in the evening - Mended clothes +c -
Thurs. 7 Bunny brought home his Kindergarten book this afternoon - Mary Wilder arrived this evening - Mr. Root also - Annie, Pater & I represented the family at prayermeeting - Letter sto Mrs. Durant, Miss Eaton & Miss Emerson - postal from Miss Emerson -

title: Marion Metcalf diary [03], 1883-1889
transcription:
125

Essays etc. by the girls - did not go.

Tues. 15 Beautiful weather.  Went to chapel - then spent morning and too lunch at Storie Hall.  Qual. class omitted today.  Faculty Meeting this evening.

Wed. 16 Clear and cool.  Classes  as usual.  Decided suddenly to go home since there are special reductions in fare for the vacation- Wrote to Lila and regrets to Mrs. Mcleary for the wedding.  Called on 4 of my section & went to prayer meeting- Worked on Qualitatur papers-

Thurs. 17. Snow in middle of day.  Snow again in evening - clear between class at 9- Went to Boston at 10-& came back at 3:45.  Carrie Soule took dinner with me-n{Gen.?} Armstrong talked at prayer meeting twice- very interesting on the Indian Work at Haupton[?] &  other where.  Letter from Pater- Cards from Lila & Mrs. Cooke her aunt.  Wedding invitation from Hattie Emerson-

title: Marion Metcalf diary [03], 1883-1889
transcription:
Went to village with Miss Gates and Miss Cooley. Made Bible questions, wrote letter home and part I [[?]] one [[?]] to Ethel. Concert by Campanari Bro's. & Mr. Arthur Whiting. writ [[?]] not.
Tues. 26 Considered Bible Questions with the other Sophomore teacher. Tested and repaired the Mineralogy lamps. Began work on the Chemical Library. Capt. Pratl of Carlisle. Indian fame spoke this morning after the prayer meeting.
Wed. 27 Finished the work on our Library. Bible examination in P.M. lasted till 5:30 or so. Elizabeth Eliza and I then writ to the village, I writ after my patched shoes [[?]]. Miss Hurll and I tried to go to prayermeeting in the evening, but gave it up, as it was so very slippery.
Thurs. Trees covered with ice. Sleeting all day. Dr. Mackenzie preached at 11. prayermeeting (section) at 10:30. Dr. N.G. Clark spoke briefly in the evening.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [03], 1883-1889
transcription:
I had a nice very short talk with him thereafter.
Friday. Regular work again. Took up the esamination questions in Bible Class. Ice still on trees. rain still falling & freezing. walking dreadful. Miss Cooley and I waded down to the village to prayermeeting, where she made a report og the religions state of the College. Miss Eastman of Dana Hall. and Miss Townsend of the public school. We had some lemonade after our return.
Sat. 20 Letter from Peter. Ice fell from the trees while the sun was out this morning. drizzling rain again towards night. Went to Dr. Baldwin's to spend the day, & had a fine time. reached there soon after 12. and left about 6.
Class of '88 [[?]] met in C.C.'s room this evening.
Sunday Jan. 31 Bright beautiful day. Snow somewhat deep. Went to church in village and stayed to Sunday School. Dr. Warren preached at College. Prayer Meeting this evening was very good. 18 were present.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [03], 1883-1889
transcription:
[page no] 99 [/page no]

Sun 13
A beautiful day- cloudy some of the time. high wind. Went to church in village - to Flourr. Sunday Service at 4 P.M. Dr Mackinzie preached on the regular text. U.C.C. meeting in village in P. M. - The students had class prayer meetings, which I had no call to attend.  Miss Hours, Miss Cooley & I had some ginger snaps  and lemonade this evening.

Monday 14 
Finished copying Library Catalogue in A. M. - Fussed & labored at College in P.M. - also took a walk- Wrote to Mr. Steirus, Nettie & Ethel in evening - began letter to John-
distributed pears-

Tues. 15 Warm, very warm- Qual Anal- at 11:45. Bible at 2:20. I unexpectedly like my Bible class- 
Faculty Meeting in P.M. - copied lists & considered work, thereafter Watch arrived. & letter fr. Uncle George & letter from home.

Wed. 16. Qual Anal. at 11:45 - Chem. at 9:00  Quant. at 9:50. Teacher's prayer meeting in evening. Finished letter to John.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [03], 1883-1889
transcription:
[page no] 100 [/page no]

Thurs. Chem class at 9:00. Worked in Lab. thereafter. Made NH4SH most of the day & evening - cleared out box of iron stuff. Went to prayer meeting.

Fri. 18  Hair lived through the day, though neither of my classes was a brilliant success - Went to walk with E. E. after 4. found cranberries & e and lost my knife - Brief letter from John - Early to bed-

Saturday Sept. 19  Beautiful weather. Went early to College to see about prayer meeting. Class at 9:00. Worked in Laboratory preparing H2S cupboards. Read articles on Energy and Molecules. Taught Elizabeth Eliza's 1:30 class- Made Bible topics- swept and dusted room- Sent letter to Annie. Rec'd letter from Annie- Ate crackers and jelly with Miss Hours. Walked to village after dinner with Miss Fuller and Miss Manning - Horticultural Show in Boston closed yesterday - Miss Easton and Cassius went to Boston Today-

title: Marion Metcalf diary [03], 1883-1889
transcription:
[page no] 101 [/page no]

Sunday. 20. Prof Bowne preached at the College. I went to village church to U. C. C. Corruant meeting, where I had the desired interview with Mr. Steirus - and to section meeting.  Only 12 girls were at the prayer meeting, rather to my disappointment, but it was a good meeting-

Monday  Walked to village in A. M. with Miss Hours - wrote to Harl and to Harry. went up to College and directed Marion Smith in some domestic work- Studied Qual. Anal. and Gen. Chem. - Retired from public life in the evening -  Sophomore and Special Receptions this evening- Read Old Maids Paradise-

Tues. 22  Did not go to breakfast, but taught classes, to all appearance successfully, at 11:45 and 2:20 - Crain's U.F. A. of the W. arrived this morning- & I sent John a Postal Note in payment for the same.  Made Bible

title: Marion Metcalf diary [03], 1883-1889
transcription:
[page no] 102 [/page no]

Ethics. Miss Cooley, Caswell, Marsh, Hours and I read some in "The Unseen Universe," by Stewart and Tait, this evening, and had a little carnal refreshment thereafter. much needed. Rain in eve.

Wed.  Cold. a few flakes of snow in P. M. classes at 9 & 11:45- Did not got to prayer meeting in the evening. Letter from home.

Thurs. 25 Miss Freeman gone to Bryn Mawr. Still cold, but bright in P.M.  Foiled & moiled in Lab- most of day. trials with bottles, stoppers, [[?]] foil, iron, iron pincers & e-
Went to prayer meeting- Wrote Lilla Davidson Patterson & to Pater - brief epistles both.


Friday Sep. 26  Beautiful autumn day - classes
as usual. Went to village after Bible class with E. E. & Miss gelstow and to prayer meeting in the evening. Made Bible topics - studied Maxwell's Theory of Heat.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [03], 1883-1889
transcription:
[page no] 103 [/page no]

Saturday Sep. 26th  Lovely weather. classes at 9 and 9:50. Put out 3 unknowns all around for Qual. Class- read paper, brushed up room - Went after gentians with Elizabeth Eliza, and found some- Letter from Susie - Wrote to Miss Glidden, and to Wilder and Mary - Sewed on my bed cover and pillows-


Sunday Sep. 27   An unusually beautiful day. Warm- Church in village- went with Miss Hours and Miss Cooley.  Mr. Eastman preached - a sermon which I greatly enjoyed. Section meeting this evening.  only 7 present, besides Miss Hattie Damon and myself - Miss Hours and I had some crackers and jelly after prayer meeting -

Monday 28   Went to Boston at 8 with Misses Marsh, Caswell and Gelstow - tried to go to Feast of Tabernacles at Synagogue on Warrenton St, but found the Synagogue closed. - Had a good dinner at the Oriental Coffee House, on washington St., came

title: Marion Metcalf diary [03], 1883-1889
transcription:
[Page No.] 104 [/Page No.]

out at 5:25. Was unable to find a screen for my room.  Mr. Bickwell did not appear to give his lecture on Alaska this evening - Rev. John Chandler and wife were here. I met them for a few minutes - Marion Sheldon came up to see me & Miss Manning and I walked to the station with her -  The whole table came up to see my opening after supper-

Tues. 29  Did not go up to chapel, but studied here until about 10:30. Did not have a very good time in either of my classes today - Went to walk with Elizabeth Eliza after Bible class. Made Bible topics in evening- Letters from Louie and from John-


Wed. 30  Classes as usual.  Home early.  Went to walk. wrote letter Louie. Made 6 calles between dinner and silent time, finding 5 people out - Florence Soule was in. Prayer meeting led by Miss Gelstow.  Miss Freeman not present-

Thurs. Oct. 1.  Lovely weather - Class at 9.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [03], 1883-1889
transcription:
[Page No.] 105 [/Page No.]

Lunch at 11:45. Walked to village, but did not meet Mr. Ernest Flagg.  Went to sleep, wh. made me very tired. studiedn Qual. and Quant. Read Christian Union. Went to prayer meeting here at Stone Hall.

Friday Oct 2   Mr. Moody holding meetings in Newton. Special Postal Delivery went into effect Wed. Sep. 30 -  Gray day- a little drizzling rain occasionally.  Classes as usual - went to village with Miss Cooley - could not get a pew in church, as Mr. Shattuck is gone to Chicago - went to see Miss Chandler and Miss Cummings for a few minutes. Miss Hours and Snead The Tinted Venus for a little while after dinner.  studied Bible, Qual. Anal- and Gen. Chem. in evening-

Sat. 3.  Gray and rainy all day. Prof. Churchill read here this P. M. from the benefit of the Monroe Elocution Fund, founded by Miss Cummin. ata this end of her 25 years of teaching.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [03], 1883-1889
transcription:
[Page No.] 106 [/Page No.]

He read.  Dickens' Dr. Marigold.

Sandy McDonald's Signal-
Dante gabriel Rosetti's Sister Helen-
No. 5 College Street.

We mended and read Jackanapes in Katherine's room this evening-  Letters from Pater, Will Metcalf and Solomon John Peterkin Duffies Van Pelt.

Sunday Oct. 4  Windy and gray and blue by spells- Dr. J. R. Miller preached at W. C. - Communion Service -  I heard Mr. Corvan at the village. taught Mrs. Dana's S.S. class.  made a few remarks in the Missionary meeting at the college. Miss Sampson, who has been teaching in Utah, spoke. Miss Freeman a note from Mrs. Durant, with something from a sister missionary about Gertrude  Chandler. Miss Hours told me some of her Pittsfield experiences.


Monday Oct 5   Beautiful weather. Went to Boston at 8, having tried in vain to find a companion to go to Nantasket or anywhere with me  came out at 2:15 - cut my 24 napkins

title: Marion Metcalf diary [03], 1883-1889
transcription:
[Page No.] 107 [/Page No.]

for Miss Glidden, wrote to John and to Susie- found letter from Annie and Normal Lesson from Mr. Denning - Memorial Service anniversary of Mr. Durant's death. Miss Freeman spoke-about Mr. Durant. Dr. Webb was present and made brief remarks.

Tues. 6  Classes as usual. Faculty meeting in evening, at wh. I made bold to speak of the time of section meetings, all myself. Wrote to Will Metcalf.

Wed 7  Worked in Lab. nearly all day. Classes at 9-9:50 & 11:45

Thurs 8  After my class, made NH4SH, gave out unknowns & did other laboratory work till late in P. M. 

Fri. 9  Christian Association meeting last night-  Today after Bible, went to village & engaged a seat in church, for Miss Morgan, Miss Cooley and myself-  Read "Tinted Venus" with Miss Hours &  sewed one window cushion this evening.  Made Bible topics. Went to see Ada Ayer.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [03], 1883-1889
transcription:
[Page No.] 108 [/Page No.]

Sat. 10  More laboratory work. Went to village with Marion Marsh. Swept room. finished "Tinted Venus" and one window cushion-
Lovely weather-

Sun. 11  Went to church in village with Miss Cooley, Miss Gates & Loyd the elevator boy. Section meeting this evening at Stone Hall- 10 present and a good meeting - Went up to College after it, to see Elizabeth Eliza & Miss Tuttle - Miss Hours and I then had some chocalate-

Mon. 12  Went to Boston with Elizabeth Eliza & Cassius Caius &  went out to Crescent Beach, where we had a good time, sitting in the sun and looking at the ocean - came back into the city at 12:12. Took dinner at Marston's - went to Antique Bookstore & to Cupples & Upham's - I came out at 2:15 and went to College to attend to the H2S generators.  Made cover for window cushion and studied chemistry & Bible lesson.  No letters- Beautiful day - Concert this evening- piano & Herr Karl Faeten

title: Marion Metcalf diary [03], 1883-1889
transcription:
[Page No.] 109 [/Page No.]

Tues. 13

75th Anniversary of A. B. C. F. M. opened this afternoon- classes as usual. Lu Upton & the Rev A. G. came out here this afternoon. I had quite a nice visit with them., fr. 3:10, after Bible, until they took the coach at 4:45. Annie Sawyer brought a lady into my Bible class. Read some this evening with Misses Hours, Caswell & Cooley & covered one of my new little pillows-
Letters fr. Ethel, John & Pater - all brief-

Wed. 14  Omitted Qual. class today - taught Lottie's 1:30 class. Went to Boston at 3:39 with Miss Marsh & Miss Gelstow to Fin. Board meeting - escaped with our l?irs from the crowd, had good seats, heard Dr. Stows & came out at 9:00- 

Thurs. 15  Did not go to Boston in A. M. because liable to teach Lottie's 1:30 class.  Went however, at 1:53. After making NH4SH, went to A. B. C. F. M. at 4:00 & at 7:00 - heard Dr. Hopkins, Pres. Bartlett, Prof. Fiske of Chicago- & some reports of C[?]- came out at 9:00-

title: Marion Metcalf diary [03], 1883-1889
transcription:
Fr. 16. Left my NH4SH to go and attend to Rev. Archibald Hadden - showed him about the house & enjoyed him much.  was thereby late to Quant. Class. After lunch, met Rev. Jas. Brand, Prof. Newton, Prof. Ballantine & Mr. Jas. Fairchild - Prof. Ballantine lectured on "The Land of Moab"- at 2:20- not very good, to my mind.

Sat. 17  Work as usual in A. M. - brushed and dusted room. Went rowing with Miss Knox and Miss Cordeman at 4- The table came up with this evening & sewed on apron for Miss Glidden's school. & read Jackanapes - Chem. Ed. at 9:00-

Sun. 18  On the bed all day. Meals sent up. read Christian Union & Am. Board reports.  Dr. Harry preached.

Mon. 19.  Did not go to breakfast- Wrote to Harl and Ethel - Marion Marsh came down in P. M. 

Lecture this evening by Dr. Cyrus Hamlin on "Present Condition of Turkey."

title: Marion Metcalf diary [03], 1883-1889
transcription:
Tues. 20. Classes & Laboratory labors as usual. Faculty meeting in evening. 

Wed. 21. Written lesson in Qual. Anal- also one in Quant. Anal.
Rain in evening. went not to prayer meeting - Wrote home- and to Edith.

Thurs. 22  Rev. Frank white, from London, Eng, gave an illustrated lecture on The Tabernacle of Moses - and interspersed views of roses and lilies & scripture texts wreathed around with vines and flowers & e.  Some people laughed. I will not say who - Made NH4SH.

Fri. 23  Miss Hours and I took a walk in the evening, in the full-moon light, down towards Waban Cottage. Wrote letter to Jack.

Sat. 24  Miss Weld and I walked on the aqueduct to Echo Bridge, and back by the road- Some of the girls came this evening to sew- and we read "Laddie"- Miss Hours sick & has a new gown-

Sun. 25  Fine weather.  Dr. Noah Porter was expected to preach at College today, but Mr. Lee, Chris Lee's father, came instead. I went to church & S. S. - in the village.  Sophomores had a Union prayer

title: Marion Metcalf diary [03], 1883-1889
transcription:
[Page No.] 112 [/Page No.]

meeting this evening, & a very good one.

Mon. 26  Wrote to Annie - finished 3 gingham aprons for Indians in Miss Glidden's school. studied Bible & Qual. Anal. tried to take a nap.  we had a Faculty Meeting in Mrs. Harrison's room after supper - quite amicable, but not very satisfactory.
Organ recital by Prof. Whiting - went not
A case of smallpox in Natick-
Letter from Pater- Miss Harper came to my room to take an examination.

Tues. 27  Fog again morning & night. Classes as usual.  Postal fr. Lilla D. Patterson

Wed. 28  Mr. & Mrs. Smith, missionaries of A. B. C. F. M.  Fr. Shantung, China, talked in chapel, wh. began at 8, For those who cared to come - They spoke again in teachers' prayer meeting.
exceedingly interesting.  Went to Natick.

Thurs. 29  Prepared for Marsh's Test for As. Mr. Smith led prayers this morning. Mrs. Smith talked at the meeting this evening.  Went to village in rain with Miss Cooley.  I was vaccinated on Tuesday.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [03], 1883-1889
transcription:
[Page No.] 113 [/Page No.]

Friday  Letter from Harl- & Family Story Paper. wh. made me feel insulted -
Did Marsh's test for As in P.M. - with some of the girls - in safety-
Miss Cooley & I went to Preparatory Lecture in village this evening - Rain-

Sat. 31  Marsh's test again - Classes as usual  
Letter from Annie - Four girls came to sew & we read E. P. Roe's story from the Christian Union- Halloween Party this evening - Miss Hours & I rigged up and went down but came to grief and stayed only 3 or 5 minutes-
Swept room - Went to village with Marion Marsh and Mdlle - See-

Sun. Nov 1  Cold & gray- Communion Sunday in village church.  I taught (very poorly) the Primary Class in the Sunday School.  The table sang hymns in Miss Hours' room after supper.  Missionary Meeting this evening to wh. I did not go-

Mon. 2  Rain & wind.  Partially clear in P. M. 
Marsh's test - wrote home & to Uncle George - 
Studied & e. Lecture  by Mr. Bolles, of Salem, on

title: Marion Metcalf diary [03], 1883-1889
transcription:
[page no.] 114 [/page no.]

Microscopic Forms of Plant Life - did not go. finished napkins for Miss Glidden-

Tues. 3  Classes - Bible class as usual. Qual. class omitted today- so I spent the morning and took lunch at Stone Hall.  Half of Miss Caswell's section came in with mine today.  Went to walk with Miss Marsh and Miss Yelstow after after Bible -
Letter from home. Faculty meeting this evening. Miss Freeman has a very bad cold, and was not there.  Election Day-

Wed. 4  Classes as usual. Puttered around in Laboratory until 4 o'clock- walked over to Mrs. Durant's with the Wise Lady.  Went with Miss Hurll to prayer meeting led by Miss Chapin, only 9 present.  Beautiful Day. Canon Farrar lectures on Dante in Tremont Temple this evening-

Thurs. 5  Christian Association meeting the evening. Canon Farrar lectured in Boston on Browning.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [03], 1883-1889
transcription:
[page no.] 115 [/page no.]

Fri-6.  Discussed the Sunday question somewhat in Bible class today. Marion Marsh and I went to walk together thereafter. A fine warm day- Letters from Pater and Jack, also one from Lilla D. Patterson, which came to Katherine, but was to me equally.


Sat. 7.  Went to Boston at 11. bought a cloak, wh. some of my friends say does not fit - heard Dr. Meredith on Jonah and the whale. Letter from Edith, enclosing the money for Mio Howard.  Our club met in Miss Hours' room- and read "Through the Looking Glass"-

Sun. 8.  Grey. Foggy and rainy. Miss Cooley and I went to church, late, and heard a good sermon on Assurance.  Dr. Courtney, of St. Paul's Church, Boston, preached at the College morning and evening-  We had some chocolate in Miss Howes' room.

Mon. 9.  Gray & rainy, but cleared towards night. Wrote to Pater, Harl & Ethel. Went to Boston with Miss Hours & Miss Cooley, to change my cloak & e.  urut at 11- came out at 2:15

title: Marion Metcalf diary [03], 1883-1889
transcription:
[page no.] 116 [/page no.]

Concert this evening by the Beethoven String Quartet of Boston - went not.
Tues. 10 Lovely weather. Qual. class omitted again, so I spent morning & took lunch at Stone Hall - Letters from Uncle George & Cains Cassius  Kendall- & Pater. Read "In Tennessee Mts." in evening with Miss Hours & Miss Cooley.
Wed. 11. Wrote to Pater about Non Partisan Temperance Documents - classes as usual. Did explosion experiment with Miss Fuller. Made calls on Edith Wilkinson & Miss Slater. Miss Edith Sturgis came to see me. Went to prayer meeting, Miss Currier led it.
Thurs. 12 Warm again - Went to village to take shoe to be mended - Miss Marsh and Miss Yelston came to see me, and we talked about Bible lesson. Went to prayer meeting here at Stone Hall - Wrote to John - Letter from Pater -
Fri 13 - Classes as usual - Qual. had an ed. and did miserably - Did not have a good time in Bible class.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [03], 1883-1889
transcription:
117

Sat. 14. Classes - swept and dusted room.

Read on quantitative experiment - table girls came here to sew in evening. Miss Hours and I took a walk by the Charles River in the afternoon.

Sun. 15 - In bed all day. Miss Hours & Miss Cooley sick also - Carrie Soule and her sister came to see me in P.M. of day. Corrected qualitative papers and meditated on that class.  Studied Bible lesson.  Read Mr. Whites’ book on The Tabernacle.  Marion Marsh came to see me.

Tues 17 - Clear, cold weather.  Taught classes.  Letter from Ethel and one from house.  Went to Faculty meeting in evening, where Miss Godfrey instructed about the Library Classification. 

Wed. 18 - Classes - Prayer meeting led by Miss Tuttle.  Miss Cooley and I took a ride this afternoon.  Very good in Mr. Cheney’s grounds.  Consulted Mr. Crawford about sending things to Dakota to Miss Glidden.

title: Marion Metcalf diary [03], 1883-1889
transcription:
Thurs. 19 Led prayer meeting at College-
a Bible Reading on "the victory that overcometh the world"- Miss Hours and I went to Waban Cottage to dinner, had to go late and leave early on account of my prayer meeting - came back in a snow storm, the first of the season. 
Friday Nov. 20 [Gar Qual Class another exam- [ination] on classes I, II, & III - Corrected written work of Geo. Chem. class.  Went to village to prayer meeting with Miss Jackson- a beautiful cold moonlight night. 
Sat. 21 Did quantitative Experiment- Alum- worked at packing the box for Miss Glidden- unpacked in a barrel first, then took everything out + put into a box, which must now wait for the pinchushions to come from Natick - Read Howells' Farce - "The Gamotters" at the meeting this evening- + finished up six of the Dakota aprons-
Sunday 22 Very tired- did not get up to breakfast- Miss Hours came up and

transcription:
Gilman’s Station N.T.
April 23rd 1865

Colonel,

I hardly know how to begin. The prospection continues and this keeps you without pay, and to keep this particular, but will endeavour to be as brief as possible — Our friend Major O’Brien has received information from friends in Washington, that he can have the appointment of Col. by request if he can only get the matter properly before the War Dept.

I had a long talk with him in regard to this prospect, and the only way that it can be done in my opinion is through your aid, through the Commanding Officer. If you will make the recommendation and forward through the intermediate channels to the War Dept., I think it will be successful, for I believe that your Government interest will meet with Government approval at the War Dept. He has, we found before, the support from his portion there afterward & I feel sure that it will be received full

title: Robert R. Livingston letters, 1864-1865
transcription:
and will be of great benefit to the Major in his future career, in both military and civil life.

If you can make such a recommendation, it will give great satisfaction to many of his numerous friends. I give a slight history of the Major’s career since the war began, which may be of service to you if you should see fit to make the proper document.

On the 4th of April 1861, he (Mr. O'Brien), then in Washington, was one of the patriotic Union men, that helped to raise & form men there called the Clay Battalion, the Allegiance of our national capital. He served as a private soldier until the organized system was introduced and by order of the Sec’y of War he was then appointed to a position in the army as a post officer at Sedgwick, D.C.

On the 9th of August 1862 on receipt of the news that his brother Capt. Thomas J. O'Brien of Missouri Infantry had been killed at the battle of Cedar Mountain, Maj. O'Brien tendered his resignation in the commissary's dept., left office and proceeded forthwith to Washington, where he obtained authority from the Sec’y of War to raise and equip Reg't in the State of Iowa, which was

title: Robert R. Livingston letters, 1864-1865
transcription:
ratified by the Govr. of Iowa. And O'Brien commissioning Col. on the 16th of Sept 1863 (of the 42nd Iowa Infty).
He spent about $4000 in endeavouring to raise the said regt. but only succeeded in raising 5 or 6 companies. Thence a consolidation with the 43rd Iowa Infantry, was ordered by the War Dept, and by Mutual Consent S. W. [[?]] was appointed Col O'Brien Lt. Col. of what was to be known as the [[7?]] Iowa Cavl.
The Organization was not yet a full Cavalry Regt and all being anxious to get into Active service. It was postponed to Lt Col O'Brien to unite with Major Patter's Batt- of the 41st Iowa and give Major Patter the Position of Lt Col OBrien deeming it for the good of the service that the Regimented organization should be immediately completed connected to the proposition and accepting the position of Major. Though he had been in command as Col and Lt Col and had raised and organized a majority of the Regiment, as soon s fully organized the Regt was ordered to the western frontier and major OBrien was stationed with a command at [[Cattormany?]] Spring & the Fort Benson as Post [[Cattormany?]] was [[?]] and constructed under the direction of the Major + the manual Cabin [[?]]

and was burried at 7 churches in Kings Co. near the "Shannon" the family burying place, of the people; the Gannons. As I was only a small child, have only faint remberance how she looked. Have been told she was an Ecellent  person, and good looking women, and greatly esteemed by all the acquaintances for her fine qualties.
These were the years of the Potato Rot in Ireland; when people died on the highways, and hedges, of hunger, and diseases consequent to famine; people became rebellous in consequent of the treatment of the English Government; instead of giving them food they filled the Land full of "Peelers" and "Red Coats" when the poor people were afraid when the gathered to bury their dead they might be arrested! assembling against the proclamations of + the King or rather "Queen Victoria" [see notes PAGE IIII] Father's cousins Thomas and Stephen Hanson who came to America when young men; then living in [[Chiloupe?]] Ohio; learning of the conditions in Ireland; sent money back to their father to pay the family's passage to where the were then living in Iowa, and enough to passage of father and his children, to New York, where father had a relation living; we came to the U.S. spring 1849. The Hansons started for Iowa, but we stopped in Jersey City; father finding work. In Buffalo N.Y. uncles Michael and John Gannon (my mother's brothers) lived, we stopped a while; with them; then took passage on a Lake steamer around the lakes to Chicago, where father had a friend, we stayed short time, when we came in freight wagon to Dubuque Iowa! No R.R. running west from Chicago at this time!

IV
Father left us children in a boarding house and walked 80 miles to our people, the Hansons, living on what is + + Known as "old mans creek" Iowa Co. near where now the town of Williamsburg, when Ed. Hanson came with father for us with a wagon drawn by pair of oxen! We stayed about year when we came to Iowa City then the Capitol of Iowa. Father found work, after few years he found a job clerking a grocery ice store and keeping the books after many years working in this store he secured imployment in a seed and agriculure implement house where worked until retired on account of age, then he lived with his different children. he died Dec. 19. 1881 at Iowa City, his home for many years; and buried on family Plot in the Catholic cemetery among his old friends
- NOTES -
+ In 1848 Rebellion broke in Counties of Tipperary, Wicklow, when Smith O'Brien, John Martin, Jas. Dillon, and Thomas Francis Meagher were arrested and transported to Australia, they were rescued few years after! Same Thomas Francis Meagher, that was Major Genl. in Civil 1861-1865 and distinguished himself in the "army of the Potomac"
++ At this date 1849 this settlement of the Hanons was, with exceptions of few families living on the Desmoines river where were stationed troop of U.S. Cav. when the present City of Desmoines stands. farthest West, to the Pacific Ocean! The mormons this year moved to the Mo. River and named their stopping place Kanesville on their journey to Salt Lake, now Council Bluffs, Iowa.

title: Martin J. Feenan papers, 1864-1920
transcription:
V
Father's sisters Mary, Rose, Catherine, never came to America I believe Aunt Rose became a nun Aunt Mary married a Mr. Dillon and lived at Moat Co. Westmeath Aunt Catherine +++ married and lived with parents on the old homestead until they died at great age! I heard Grand Mother lived near 90 yrs of age! Uncle Thomas, and aunts Eliza, and Ann, Came from Ire to Iowa City 1853, and aunt Margaret, who had married Patrick Byrne about 1848, and came to America living at Cahoes N.Y. came in 1854, also to Iowa City and the brothers and sisters in America were again united.
Uncle "Tom" learned the brick and plastering trade at Iowa City, and during the Civil went to Conn. Hartford and New Haven, he never married! made several trips to Ireland and brought, nephews and nieces over which he helped to educate and found employment for them Uncle "Tom" whom I knew well; was well read and had fair eduction, and showed much good breeding and polish; was esteemed by his companions for social, genial disposition; died at Hartford Conn. a good age, and buried at E. Hartford Catholic Cemetery Aunt Eliza, married John Woodward, at Iowa City and soon after moved to Milwaukee Wis. where they lived until their death at old age, and burried in family plot catholic cemetery, there; they had family of 2 girls who grew up Eliza & Mary Ann married and they had children
Aunt Ann, married Patrick Byrne in Iowa City a Blacksmith; they had 5 children 2 boys Martin and James 3 girls, Eliza, Ann Margaret - Mary- they married and had children sons learned to be machinists; Martin, never married! James married and raised a family.

title: Martin J. Feenan papers, 1864-1920
transcription:
VI
Aunt Ann died at Chicago; lived quite old 65 yrs; was buried in catholic cemetery there (Chicago)
Aunt Margaret lived many years at Iowa City, after death of her husband! when she married John Brady, of Keota Keukuk Co. Ia, a farmer, when she and her husband got very old sold farm and moved to Iowa City made arrangements with sisters there to care for them during their lives! Aunt Margaret never had children! she and her husband Brady, are burried in St Marys Cemetery there, Aunt Margaret beside her first husband "Byrne" and "Brady" next her one other side and all have Hdstones, marking grass.
- NOTES -
+++
The Home of Grand Father have a faint recolection as I was only small boy when I last seen it, 6 or 7 years old; a long stone house with an L on the so. side 1 1/2 storey faced west on national Highway which was paved with stone and trees planted on each side, grain barn, where the wheat and oats were stacked; stood on south side of front yard, grain was thrashed with a flail! on north stood the stables where the cattle were housed; the house stood well back from the road. In rear was a beautiful yard filled with grass and shrubery surrounded by a blackthorn hedge; am told my father kept this nicely trimmed; different kinds of Roses and lialacs along the sides and Roses trailed on the stone wall of house my father had made a sundial which was in hedge and the hedge trimmed even, could tell time; when sun shone

title: Martin J. Feenan papers, 1864-1920
transcription:
VII
- JAMES H. FEENAN -
My brother James H. Feenan, was what might be called a "self-made man"! Handicapped as us "Boys" were, father having for first years in Iowa City done labor's work, and the poor price paid those years was hardy enough to feed and clothe, motherless children and keep us together, we only got 3 or months schooling winter time James was a bright boy, and learned easily, and studied home nights and Sundays fathers teaching us! The Law firm of Edmunds and Ransom took him in their office to keep things in order, (he being so neat in his appearance,) and orderly, they soon were so attached to the Boy, and he being a fine penman they had him read Law in their office he soon got so he done their coping and writing legal forms (no type writers, in these days) Mr Ransom helped, so that before he had been in their office 2 1/2 years he passed fir examination, and was admitted to the Bar. Lawyer friend opened an office in Marengo (Co. Seat Iowa Co.) and took him in partnership! He soon built up a Living practice and his business increased so took in partners. "Feenan, Hughes and Kirk" and he was considered finest Equity lawyer in his Judicial District! James married in 1866 Laura Kidd who lived in Dubuque Iowa, they had six children 2 Boys 4 girls Fanny, Fred, Florence, May, Eva, James and Laura, younger children died when small children, Brother gave them fine schooling; Fanny, married a Mr. Vance and raised fine family Fred, became a Lawyer and Married; had 2 daughters. Mrs. Feenan soon after husbands death sold her interests in Marengo and moved with her daughters Florence and Mary Eve to Los Angeles Calf. she is there at this date. Brother James died from an incurable Disease in Prime of Life, in Chicago 1906, about 64 years of age and burried besides his children on family lot at Marengo Iowa

title: Martin J. Feenan papers, 1864-1920
transcription:
VIII
- SISTER MARY -
Sister Mary was a grand woman; when girl 10 years she kept house for father and us "Boys" staying out of school most of the time and kept a home for us until we grow up and left home kept house for father until she married and father lived with for a time. After her marriage to Albert Clifton she went to Deadwood So. Dakota and opened Dressmaking and Millinery business in connection with the shoe business of Mr. Clifton, who was a shoemaker. Mr Clifton dieing, she married after a time a Mr. Fox! when her health failing she sold out and she and Mr. Fox moved over the line to Crook Co. [[loys?]] built a flouring mill nice waterpower, on sand creek. She still prospered but her health getting worse she sold the mill and went back to Iowa City for treatment! after an operation she felt better for a time and returned to her home, Beulah Wyo. and died Beulah Wyo. May 8. Not sure of year. her husband, Mr Fox, carried out her request and he brought her body to Iowa City and was burried beside her father on the plot; and those 2 who dearly loved each other are united in death. The lot is curbed with marble and their graves have granite markers
- NOTES -
In session of Iowa Legislature winter 1856-1857 they Removed the capitol of the state to Desmoines and gave to state House and grounds to Iowa City for state university. Regents opened in spring '57 normal Dept state university; which the writer and brother James attended this first term and father not able to send us any more, we went to work. I speak of this; as something with honour to it, a Mrs. Stephens of [[Benson?]] who was a Miss Aylsworth of Iowa City was a member of this class. She and I believe are only ones alive

title: Martin J. Feenan papers, 1864-1920
transcription:
XIII - CONWAYS -
Robert Conway (my wife's father) was born March 31. 1815 in City Kilkenny Ireland he came from a family of small merchants known in Ireland as "shop keepers" he had fine business education; kept fine set of Books.
He married Anna O'Neill a daughter of Mr. O'Neill who conducted a hotel in city of Tramore Co. Waterford Ireland 1842. she was a woman of much education and refinement. They had 5 children (girls) Mary M. (wife) was born January 21 1843 in Tramore (as I believe) daughters Anna, and Margaret. after Margaret's birth he came to America, settleing in New Orleans where he had relatives and opened small grocery. soon after sent for family when Catherine and annastatia were born. In 1856 came to Dubuque Iowa where he had sister married to a Mr. grace a rich farmer. he opened up a wholesale Liquor Business 131 Main St. His wife dieing in 1861, married again! (year following)on discovering of Gold in Montana he crossed the plains to Virginia City returning next year 1865( in winter), spring 1866 he returned to Va. City taking his family by team except Mary! which I married on on May 1. [[?]] 1866 by Father Gannon at Cedar Rapids Iowa,and his youngest child Statia who was at convent school!after our marriage they continued their trip and we went to Iowa Citymy home. In spring 1867 after our Baby was born, Robert car. Conway sent for me to come to Montana,going by steam boat up the Mo. river! I helped him build a small Hotel  “Madison House” which is the principal House of Va. City today! Mr Conway had 4 children by his second wife Boys, Robert E Thomas Francis. Martin J and Charles. Mr Conway died Nov. 27. 1878at Va. City (and buried in Cemetery there), in his 73d year

where - as The 6th Iowa Cav. Assn. having met for the first time since “muster out” in Oct. 31.1865. At the close of the war for the Union.
Where-as This regiment was recruited in the fall of 1862 as as other Iowa troops to preserve the union of the States; but was in consequence of the Indian outbreaks of the differend bands of Sioux in the agencies and outside bands in the Minnesota river country, on Aug 1862, when they massacred the people of New Ulm Minn. and spirit Lake Iowa, and other points by the hundreds and destruction of millions of property and spread terror along the border settlements of Iowa and Minnesota
where-as The war department assigned the 6th Iowa Cav. in Genl. Sully’s command to punish those Indians and protect the frontier settlements from their raids, scalping and plunder
where-as The members of the 6th Iowa Cav. have learned that on the battlefield of white stone Hill Dickey Co. no. Dakota stands a granite monument to commemorate the great Victory of the 6th Iowa Cav. on Sept. 3, 1862 when the 6th Iowa Cav.completely routed the hostile Sioux killing hundreds of them and taking over 300 prisoners; The same savages under chief little crow who were in the massacres of Minnesota and northern Iowa, and further the project was inaugerated by comrades of Dickey Co. Oakes, North Dakota, Aug 15, 1909
Mr. M. J. Feenan
Dear Sir & Comrade: - 
You have my thanks for your very interesting story of the Battle at Whitestone Hill.
I have taken the liberty to pass it to the editor of our local paper for publication
It settles some points that were in dispute. I would like to ask what were the movements of your troops after Sept 3. - Some claim that there was fighting with the Sioux on the 5th. Your answer will settle that question. - We will put the monument on the Hill near the Whitestone which overlooks the battlefield. We reserve a park of seventy (70) acres which includes the Hill and the lake.
Now if you remember the position of the White-stone or the Hill with reference to the lake, perhaps you can give me a diagram showing the position of the Indians, of the Iowa Cav and of the Nev. Cav. and showing the retreat of the Redskins.
Perhaps too, on yr diagram you can show where the soldiers were buried. We are as yet unable to find the trenches. We find five (over)

REFERENCE TO ROSTER! [[hand symbol]] BACK

Martin J Feenan 1126 so. 32, Omaha who served as Q.M. sergeant Co. "M" 6th Iowa Volunteer Cavalry. Having receive a Roster of the Cavalry regiments who served in the Civil War from Iowa. The Legislature few years previous had voted an appropriation to furnish all soldiers, Infantry, Cavalry and Artilary, each a copy of this work, was done through General Logan then Adjt. Genl. of Iowa at Des Moines and he delegated a favorite politician to superintend this work. This man giving a short sketch of each Regt. which was followed by the names, and rank of each soldier of the 12 Companies, in the Regt.
When he came to the 6th Cav. he stated "This Regt was Raised to fight Indians "which I knew was false and could not be substanciated from any point. This matter I brought before the Reunion of the 6th Iowa Cav. at Marshalltown June 1916; by the writer who said I enlisted Aug 12th 1862 Co "I" "22" Iowa Infty and this "out Break" of the Sioux did not occur until August 20! 8 days after when they massacred the people of new relm Minn and spirit Lake Iowa took place The comrades attending did not seem to feel, as I did; that this statement was a stigma on the military accord of each soldier who served in the 6th when they enlisted, as all men of the Regiment, to save the Union! I determined to fight this matter singly if I must; when a copy of Roster produced and he read the statement, he said this man know his business! when I said he did not, and I asked the Genl if he had on file in his office an order from the war Dept at Washington

Dakotas the blood of your fathers talk to you from the graves where you stand their spirits come up to your arms and make you strong I am glad of it! Dakotas the big men are here they have Marzasha in a pin like a [[wolf?]] they mean to kill him for not letting them cheat us out of our lands and the money our great father sent us. This midnight attack was only prevented by the half-breeds and other more peaceable Indians. But the fires were not quenched; only covered with ashes.
- BISHOP WHIPPLE -
Bishop Whipple, Episcopal church, Minnesota published a pamphlet January 1863 speaking of the Indian massacre The nation has heard of the most terrible Indian massacre in history. But those who live remote from the border can have no idea of the awful horrors which have accopanied the desolation of 200 of the finest country on earth. Many of the victims of this savage ferocity were my friends. They [[minged?]] their voices with mine in prayer. They had given me such hospitality as only can be found in the log cabin of the frontier. It fills my heart with grief and blinds my eyes with tears when ever I think of their nameless graves. It is because I love them and would save others from their fate that I ask the people shall lay the blame of this great crime where it belongs and rise up with one voice to demand the reform of atricious Indian system which has always gardened for us the same fruits of anguish and blood There is not a man in America who gave an hours calm reflection to this subject who does not know that our Indian system is an organized system of robbery and has been for years a disgrace to the nation.

title: Martin J. Feenan papers, 1864-1920
transcription:
4 It was under the Indian system that the fierce war like Sioux was fitted to be actors in this bloody drama. They were taught by the white man that lieing was no disgrace. Adultry no sin and theft no crime! It has been so for 50 years it will be so again Gods retributive Justice always has compelled people to reap exactly what they have been permitted to be sown They have seen innocent women die from the brutal violence of white men They knew what ficticious  amounts were certified to and mens names placed on pay rolls
"It has been well established that this uprising and massacring of those Sioux Indians Aug, 20, 1862 was contemplated not only by the Sioux; but the chipawas, winnebagos, and wilder tribes west not in Minnesota. There had been councils held by differ chiefs on this scheme. Many of those christian Indians on reservation could talk and read English and were posted about our war It is dreadful to contemplate the distruction of lives and property. But when the hour came the winnebagos and chippawas got cold feet; and let the sioux do the massacring."
"Mr Heard tells in his book " 3 years sioux war" some of the cases are too terrible to narate. Tells of Mr Everett settler, and his little daughter finding each other after months of seperation was most affecting. His wife had been murdered and his little son 4 years old killed before his eyes and an other child younger was alive when last seen, out of this once happy family father and daughter remained The child took the hand of father and pressed it against his bosom and not a word was spoken An other little girl 9 years of age was subject to most brutal treatment by those savages Imagination can hardly depict the enormities perpetrated upon those poor women Cannot be described but awful to contemplate. They seemed to be possessed by the very demon!"
