The waitress you got for St. Regis — I hope she won't take

title: Slim Brundage letters, 1965-1972
transcription:
up the same way Rosie did with John.
Stacy keeps coming up in your life — will she be the next one to share your digs? She doesn't stick with anything very long but she is a nice person just the same.
I'm a little more comfortable now that the air-hammers have been replaced with skill saws and hand hammers. It sounds more constructive next door. Lots of new building going on here now and planned for the future. The students seem to be interested in sports this year instead of rebellion. — Too many CIA, FBI, police etc. — especially narcs — running around pretending to be students. I'm convinced that much experimenting with chemicals is going on undercover here by the government. There is too much "protection" for just holding the students in line. —— Altho we've had a pot smoke-in on the Capital steps nobody was arrested or bothered. They openly broke the law and no one did anything about it so the kids stopped bothering to get a rise out of the 'establishment'.
Writing has been a major chore for me this month. Can't get going on all the letters I owe. I'm having lots of fun reading all kinds of things. That way I feel no pain but everything gets neglected.
I do hope you stay well. You enjoy living so much. I want you to have all the joy possible. 
Love, 
Alice

title: Slim Brundage letters, 1965-1972
transcription:
May 31, 1972
117 W. Dayton
Madison, Wi. 53703
Dear Slim:
I'm so sorry you had to leave your place and move into the Marshall Hotel. It makes me scared. These things are happening to so many elderly people all over the United States and maybe all over the world. We are not wanted. The only thing people are good for is to work and spend lots of money. Old people can't do either. — Can't see that a senior citizens organization will change the state of things. People are screaming for the end of the war for years but the only thing that will end it is trade and the need of it. — Can't remember that people ever counted with government or others who have power. Still you understand how to get things done better then I do and I hope you can get better conditions this time for the elderly.
Last month I called my mother on the phone and she indicated I should come to her. So I did. She doesn't want to live any more and expects to die in a few months. She is healthy in all the vital parts so I doubt that she will succeed in losing interest enough to die. That is her attempt. Lose all desires. — The buddhists say that is the road to enlightenment. — who knows. — I cleaned everything I could find and worked all the time I was there

title: Slim Brundage letters, 1965-1972
transcription:
If I talk I get into trouble so I worked instead of talking. Even so I guess people got unhappy with me because I didn't visit them. I guess I'm always wrong with my family.
While I was in Florida there was a peace march in Madison. 10,000 people in a candle-lite walk. About 10 people started breaking windows and the police panicked. The tear gas was so thick you could't see across the street. Of course people started running away from it so the cops ran after them and hit as many as possible with their riot sticks. There were only a few arrests and the next 6 days the marches were held but only a few, like 200, participated. — So I missed all that.
Saw this article about Mexico and the disabled vets. Thought you would be interested.
I've read several articles about how the people live in China and Russia. If these stories are true it must be very nice to live there. Of course if I read some of the articles written about the U.S. I'd think this was a wonderful place to live and it isn't.
Be happy and I hope the college is doing good. Do you still have the whorehouse next to the Hotel? Is anything going on with rebuilding on La Salle? Are more blacks moving in around Division and La Salle? Are people feeling healthy, those you meet? How's Anna doing?
I'll write again, soon I hope
Love, 
Alice

title: Slim Brundage letters, 1965-1972
transcription:
June 28, 1972
117 W. Dayton
Madison Wi. 53703
Dear Slim:
As soon as you feel good you get ambitious and get involved with all kinds of  things and the people you contact are more cautious and you get irritated and your ulcer starts up again. These old people's programs to make things better have not done so and they are suspicious no. They don't believe anyone any more and don't expect anything good to happen. — Like if S.S. is raised there is much written about it but nothing is said or written about the Medicare or Medicaid card cost being raised too and wipes out almost all the gain.
Here either I'm beginning to understand things better or all is getting worse. The University of Wisconsin spend 50 million dollara a year. The corruption is so bad you can't believe it. Still no one says or does anything. The good people all leave Wisconsin — it's one of the few states that shrunk in population. The students say there are still good teachers at the technical college but I'll bet that won't last much longer. It's about 50% good teachers left. But students are not too good at judging because the lower schools all have poor teachers too. So there is nothing to compare with.
I happened to see last year's June Curriculum

There are so few chances to say anything anywhere now. Your College of Complexes I think does a real service. Do you still get angry at the meetings? The issues don't get you down it's people's intolerance to each other that usually raises your dander.

The apartment buildings that were put up here for low income people are renting for $160 a month for 1 bedroom apt. — This scares the hell out of me. All low rentals are being torn down all over U.S. and no reasonable apts in their place. There is a backlog of orders for house trailers here. There just is no place to live except the expensive places. More and more apts are vacant but the rents still go up. — What ever happened to competition? I'm scared. — Talking to the old ladies around here shows that apathy rules their lives. There are no other people to talk to but the papers Letters to the Editor show the racism and bigotry beyond belief. — When I make a world, things will be different, better!
Love,
Alice

Dear Slim:

I was in Florida for about 10 days working on my mother's very old papers and other things. Then Helen, my sister, and Mother and I went by plane to Denver. Now we decided to look for a residence for the 3 of us to live in. Looks expensive too but not impossible. 
It has rained here every day since we came on the 13th and is raining now. That's more rain then in the last 10 months.

I just hope I hear from you before you go to Mexico. Write to the Madison address and if I move soon it will be forwarded. Let me know where to write to you and I'll give you all the news from New Mexico. I'm sure I'll move out here or somewhere close by.

Then I've decided to unload the house. It is impractical for me to try to keep it alone. Have a student from Ghana staying with me temporarily, but while interesting, it is not satisfactory. We communicate badly. He does not provide any companionship - really.
Although I want to move to South Shore, I think Hyde Park is a better bet. Crime is down in Hyde Park, but up in the Shore. Also in HP, I save $40.00 a month in bus and train fares.

Mitchell is with us, goes to military school, home on

title: Slim Brundage letters, 1965-1972
transcription:
-2-
helpful to me, so will just try and pass it on.

title: Slim Brundage letters, 1965-1972
transcription:
July 1, 1971
Dear Slimbo:
Intended to write sooner about money I owe you for Mendaco. Quanto? (or is it Cuanto? in Sp.) didn't pay you when you were here because I thought we'd see you again. Are you sure that Mex. Mendaco is the same thing? It's a different color & size and I can't read the ingredients because they're not only in Spanish but also Medicalese. Do you take the same dosage: 2 at a time with full glass of water? Hart asked me about it, too, and I couldn't tell him.
We went to a barbecue at the Mitchells last Sat. supposed to be in honor of Nancy's brother & family but they had all flown back to Chicago early in the AM unexpectedly. They had news that a son of one of them (I forget which) who is a cop had been injured. So we didn't get to meet them.
The Mitchells hadn't heard from you, either and we all wondered if maybe you're sick again. Hope not. I've finished my 5 week course of physio-therapy treatmentes (traction, hot packs, & massage at $20 a whack 3 times a week) Back is much stronger and I no

title: Slim Brundage letters, 1965-1972
transcription:
2// longer have to wear the lumbar corset (which I think was making it worse) Of course my back isn't O.K and I have to see the neuro surgeon ($40 a visit) again next week. Probably means costly Xrays too. But I'm not going to have another operation unless I get helpless as I was before.
Don has had some ups and downs with his heart condition & now is back on heavy dosage of nitroglycerin. Sees his M.D. again tomorrow. But I think he should go to V.A. hospital & get a really thorough check-into. Anything wrong with his heart is really serious.
Have you seen Jane at all? I'm sending her the blouse you brought me from Mexico. It was so thoughtful of you to remember the pink – but it doesn't fit me (can't even get it on) and it's too small for Janet, too, so I thought you'd like Jane to have it if she's skinny enough. If not, maybe she can give it to her sisters or someone. Anyway it won't be wasted. Thanks just the same.
Are you doing anything about radio or TV program? Let us hear some news - and how much for the mendaco? 
Love
V & D

title: Slim Brundage letters, 1965-1972
transcription:
8/30/71
Dear Slimbo:
So glad to hear you're in such good health. Keep it up. What dood it? Give us your recipe. If it's walking, you'll be interested to know that Don's doc told him he should walk more to exercise his legs for sake of circulation. But I can't walk as I used to because it tires my back. I've given up my treatments for the past month, but will start them again now that it's cooler. We're both unhealthy but still active.
Thanks so very much for the earrings. They arrived last week – in plenty of time for my birthday (9/2) altho I don't think you knew that. I think they're stunning and very becoming. The color is fine as I wear a lot of brown but Don will have to solder some clips on instead of the weak screws. (Those Mex are so stupid. They make heavy earrings then put soft silver screws on them that won't hold. They do it every time!) Yes, I wouldn't like a red poncha [sp?] as I don't wear red. Mostly wear purple, green, orange & brown. In pastels could use lavender, yellow, tan or light green bes. Black or white OK. But I don't deserve anything more than the earrings. What can I send you? Some gray pants from Alvarado St.? What size?
The big news is from Alvarado St: Janet got married! To a new boyfriend she met while she was living at the Olympic. He lived in an apt. nearby.

title: Slim Brundage letters, 1965-1972
transcription:
We had met him only once – when we were down there to see Janet. He seems pleasant – and quite a he-man — is part-Indian (Am.) It came as a complete surprise! About 10 days ago Janet called me in the afternoon and told me she had been married that morning. I'm not yet used to the idea of her being married – after all these years. No papoose on the way yet, but I hope it's not too late for me to get a grandchild.
Well, isn't that a News Item?
Will any of your TV shows be shown out here? Let me know, so we can catch them. I've been racking my brains to think of any "unheralded good" you've done for the Chicago area. Seems to me you were always attended with trumpets. Nothing very "unsung" or "mute inglorious" about you. But seriously, I do think you've brought a lot of stimulation to a lot of different types of people – and not only brought them together for the exchange of ideas, but also (and more important) for FUN. There are a lot of stuffy or stuffed-shirt forums and discussion-groups, but only Slim put entertainment and humor in the lecture-hall. The College is a soap-box circus and I, for one, enjoyed every moment there. (How's that for a testimonial?) Glad it's going so GOOD for you.
With love V & D

title: Slim Brundage letters, 1965-1972
transcription:
Wed. Sept. 29, 1971
Dear Slimbo:
So delighted to receive the lovely poncha (is the word both m. and f. ?) Beautiful colors – will go with everything I have. Many, many thanks. Janet hasn't seen it yet, but I know she would love one — probably the brighter colors, I feel sure. The newlyweds haven't a phone, so I'm not in constant touch (which is probably just as well for a new mother-in-law) but they've been here to dinner and Janet seems happy and he seems pleasant and well-behaved - about 45. His name is Milton Lutz, but luckily they call him Tony - not Milt.
Today while book-hunting I found a little book of Rowdy Rhymes for you. Has all your favorites: Piddling Pup, Old Bankhouse, Kipling's "Ladies" etc. Will send soon. Jane said something about there being Poetry Nights again, but she didn't say were and who etc. If so, the little book will be handy.
I did not say the College was "only bullshit" – nor meant that. It's wonderful and gives a much-needed outlet for exchange of opinions and ideas. That's a serious thing; but I think much of its charm — and yourse — lies in not taking it seriously. Do you? the light touch is important, or else the College will end up being like Tunis's and other forums. If you keep it fun, everyone will come to it and go away happy and wiser. Of course, I'm proud of you, too, of you and the College! But if you take it – and yourself – too seriously, you'll end up with ulcers. Relax – and enjoy it. You've done a lot to make people happy. So be happy yourself.
How did the Gay meeting turn out? Wish I'd been there....
At the moment I can't think of any sayings for your column— but you might do one on Barbara Frietchie (sp?) "Shoot if you must"–etc. I believe she was a real person, but the incident is highly exaggerated. The best placeto look it up would be an editor's notes on the the poem in a fairly recent vol. of Whittier's poems. I'll try to find something about it if you're interested. 
It was so good to hear something about Nomi Gross, especially that she has such a good job. She was such a brilliant and darling girl. One of my favorites. I feel toward her like "a Jewish mother". I do hope she's happy. Good luck with your book.
Jane says Bill Smith and Mary Lou are splitting — at last. 
Thanks again for the lovely poncha. Didn't see anything like it in Tijuana – only junk! What an awful place! Don and I wanted to turn around and leave as soon as we got there —

title: Slim Brundage letters, 1965-1972
transcription:
But we wandered around for a while, holding our noses. I did an awfully funny thing: I remembered some good rum I had brought back from Guadalajara: Ron Castillo – so I went into the only clean-looking liquor store – almost American, with the prices clearly on the shelves and I bought a bottle of rum and a quart of vodka (Popov) all for $5.15, really a good bargain, even at Tijuana prices. So we poked along in the Customs line and when it was our turn, we innocently declared the bottles. It had never occurred to me that it was illegal, as I'd brought liquor back from Guadalajara –and that's what I told the man. But he said that was different if I'd come in on a plane (common carrier). I really don't think that it's fair to make a distinction – but I didn't argue with The Man. I was lucky that he "allowed" me (as he said) to go back to the store and get my money back. Also lucky that I'd chosen an American-type store, instead of a licor cantina (no spik) So we had to go through the long, slow Customs line twice.
Sorry you're not feeling well now. Don is much better – just had his check-up & doesn't have to go back to the Dr. for a month (instead of 2 weeks) but is still taking nitro-glyc. which is just as well as it does him so much good. Keeps his circulation going: he used to have cold feet all the time. 
My back got worse after I discontinued the treatments and I had to wear the Iron Corset while sight-seeing on the trip to San Diego. So now I'm having treatments again – three times a week, including traction – and feel better already. Hope to get out of the girdle soon.
Weather is fine now. Cool, like normal autumn "back East." 
Nancy was sick for a while: kidney infection, but was getting over it when we last saw her.
With love from both,
Virgine
P.S The new P.O. is stupider than the old one: your last letter arrived without either stamp (it had been removed) or postmark. I've also rec'd letters with uncancelled stamps (but don't tell them) On the other hand, a letter I mailed to London (AirMail 21¢) with a small enclosure was ret'd to me for full additional postage of 21¢ (42¢ altogether and it wasn't even bulky)

title: Slim Brundage letters, 1965-1972
transcription:
11/4/71
Dear Slimbo: In case Janet hasn't written to thank you (and I doubt she has, altho I'm sure you'll excuse her) she is really delighted with the poncho (fem.) which arrived safely here some time ago.
I've dreaded to tell you that her marriage almost immediately went on the rocks through no fault of hers (Poor lamb, she did so deserve to be happy at last). The Indian turned out to be a brutal alcoholic and beat her up badly. I'm proud of her that she immediately left him: it proves she's no masochist – but of course it's all very sad – altho, thank God, no papoose (which I was hoping for if all went well) Anyway, I'm sure you'll be glad that the lovely bright poncho has brougt a ray of cheer to her blasted marriage. I thank you anyway with all my heart. 
We've rec'd the invitation to your party at Nancy's and Don and I and Janet (without husband) accept with pleasure. I'll let you know on you p.c. about the Briggs. Janet will be here for dinner on Sunday & we'll try to reach them. Saturday is Hart Mitchell's birthday and Don & I are going to his party. They're all well except Nancy who does too much and tires easily. 
I know you'll be glad that Don is continuing well – only sees the M.D. now for monthly check ups altho still taking the Nitro-bid which really seems to agree with him in every way: circulation, relaxation – even disposition. But I may have to have the Operation on my disk after all. I'm taking traction treatments until Dec 1st when the neuro-surgeon is going

title: Slim Brundage letters, 1965-1972
transcription:
to examine more thoroughly. But if surgery is on the books I'm going to postpone until after New Year's anyway – and as long thereafter as possible. 
We've had another sadness besides Janet's marriage: our darling cat, Max, suddenly got sick with terrible pain. The vet said it was a blockage in his bladder and that it would recur – not really curable – so we made the tragic dexision to have him put out of pain (euthanasia). We miss him terribly. Still can't get used to his being gone.
Well, I'm sorry to have so much bad news to write, but might as well get it all over with in one letter.
Actually in spite of so many depressing things we still survive and get around. Now that it's cool we've started working on the house in Altadena – so we're busy and seldom home except evenings – altho tomorrow evening we're going to anniv. party for some neighbors & Sat. to Hart's birthday. Sorry we can't hear you "debate" at the College. Sock it to the Padre! (Why so many "fathers"?) I'm enclosing program of lectures out here so you can see how superior are the offerings at the College. How about a Branch out here?
News items: 1 the 39¢ Place (gay bar) is now gone. Don't know when or how 2 the Green Lantern in Pasadena is now a tourist restaurant. That section is coming along as an "Old Town" tourist trap - but the underground press book store that started it is all gone. Alas, Reform is making everything dull!
With love
V & D

title: Slim Brundage letters, 1965-1972
transcription:
May 31, 1972
Dear Slim:
Tragic news from the Mitchells! This evening Nancy phoned to tell me that her dear little daughter, Susie, died yesterday suddenly and after a very brief illness. Also to tell you that she didn't get your cards etc. because she was in Hawaii so she hasn't answered you etc. — but she will later. I didn't know that Nancy was in Hawaii (for about 3 weeks, I believe) until I got a card just before she returned — shortly after the 15th, I think it was. So I didn't know what had become of you until I recd your p.c. on the 22nd. Your pkge came shortly after so last Sunday (the 28th) I called Nancy to tell her about the purse. She wasn't home and Hart's son, Pete, answered the phone. He said Nancy and Hart had gone to the hospital to see Susie. I asked about her illness but he said they didn't know yet. Of course, I didn't think of death in relation to someone so young.
So altho I wasn't entirely unprepared

title: Slim Brundage letters, 1965-1972
transcription:
2//
for today's news, it certainly was a shock — and will be to you, too. Dear sweet, brave little Susie! But of course she was so frail, she was a pushover for any disease. Nancy still doesn't know exactly what it was, so I gathered, and the onset was apparently sudden. As yet I don't know any details to write you.
The funeral will be Friday. Tomorrow they are having the viewing, as Nancy called it, in Santa Monica and Don and I and Janet will go over to the funeral home, where I expect we will hear more about it, but I want to get this note off to you before then. Don will mail it tomorrow AM.
I will take the purse over to Nancy tomorrow. She never got my message about it from Pete (I expect everyone was too worried etc. Sun. night) but I told her today — and I'm sure both you and I hope it will help to cheer her a bit. I'm sure she's desolate as she was so devoted to her little crippled daughter. Luckily, the boy, Mitch, is already going to military school, so at least he won't be completely at loose ends, and will have some distraction to take his mind off it. But he's a very sensible boy.

title: Slim Brundage letters, 1965-1972
transcription:
3//
I hadn't any idea that my thank-you note to you was going to be so sad. It was terribly sweet and thoughtful of you to remember about the pink ("shocking pink") blouse — and IT FITS!! Of course I've long since outgrown the shocking pink pants I wore the other blouse with, but I'm sure I'll be able to buy something to cover my lower parts with. Anyway, it's a great success and I love it. Muy gracias (? in Italian molto grazie) Speaking of my size, I'm today on a liquid diet (I've been going on it 3 times a week, almost every other day) but so far haven't lost more than 2 lbs. as it's only a good excuse for more martinis and an ice cream soda (i.e. a "black cow": root beer with ice cream mashed in it) which I wouldn't otherwise drink. But I have more cholesterol in my blood than I should have, so the liquid (except the ice cream) cuts out all the fat solids. Otherwise I'm getting along OK — my back is very much better — never will be perfect due to the old operation, but I am getting limber again — altho I don't dare exercise much to get the fat off. Don is about the same: heart under control.

title: Slim Brundage letters, 1965-1972
transcription:
4//
Sorry you had to go straight home from Mex, in such a tizzy. I had heard a little of it from Jane, but not about Bill Smith. She said the landlord had gotten after "the girls." (Your harem, I assume) Anyway, I hope you'll get it straightened out OK.
Thank God, I'm not a "landlady" any more (most hated class on earth!) and never will be again. It's worth paying exorbitant taxes & utility bills on an empty house just not to have tenants (who are actually the lowest lice alive!) It looks like I'll die owning the Altadena house & someone else will inherit the problem. But I inherited quite a few problems myself so why not pass it along?
We had a hot spell ove the Mem. Day weekend (good for the working classes both here & in Moscow) but it's now cooling off.
With love from all
Virgine
Had my new little coal-black cat (she looks like a seal) spayed. She's recovering O.K and where have all the tom cats gone?

7/28/72
Jane wrote me about Pat Tunis. Very sorry to hear. Jane also said you read a poem at his memorial service. What poem? Am very curious.
Talked to Nancy today. She's being very brave — and is kept busy being administrator & guardian for little Mitch.
I was quite sick for the past 2 weeks. Was bit by a virus which went to my chest (thought I might get pneumonia) as well as my bum sinuses. Took antibiotics etc. and am better now altho I have to avoid air-conditioning — and we've been having a heat wave (in the 100°s) We were planning a little jaunt to San Diego but will wait till I'm 100% OK.
At least my back is better — as I've had quite a Rest. Hope you're settled satisfactorily.
Love from all
V & D

title: Slim Brundage letters, 1965-1972
transcription:
[corporate letterhead: Prentice-Wright Company
A Division of General Enterprises, Inc.
GArfield 2-3714
2149 Cushing Street
Helena 14, Montana]
Aug. 30, 1972
Dear Slimbo: This is a sheet of Janet's old practice paper for typing. She has finally quit the Office Rat Race where she never should have been in the first place as typing etc. made her so nervous. She's taking a course for Practical Nursing. (When she was young I always tried to get her to train for nursing. She could have been an R.N. all this time – but mothers never know anything!) Anyway she hasn't gone back to that bloodthirsty Indian husband.
I was so touched by the pitch in your last letter: not enough to eat, dying of thirst without booze and not even a dime for carfare, that I'm enclosing a check for 5 bucks. (For carfare, mind you, or a cup of coffee only) Seriously, I was really touched by your sending Janet the poncha for her marriage – (and I know you are as sorry as I am that she didn't find happiness at last) so I want to repay you a little for all of your thoughtful gifts. We both enjoy our ponchas so much. We wear them as mother-daughter outfits when we go to art exhibits etc. together. I finally found a shocking pink skirt to go with the blusa rosada (I looked this up in Spanish dictionary) I remember when I was 19 in Germany looking in all the shops for a weiss mantel (a white coat) Ended up having to buy one with red trimming.
We're having another heat wave – after a very slight earthquake the other night. It was supposed to rain(!) tonight on acct. of a hurricane off the coast – but it hasn't. Anything could happen. Don had to go to hospital. last month on acct. his heart but is OK now; Janet has dizzy spells from low blood pressure and I take aldomist for high blood pressure (have for 3 years) Also have asthma. [begin marginal insertion] My Swedish grandfather died of asthma before he was 50. Went to Denver for it, but it didn't help. [end marginal insertion ] (still take Mendaco – but the Mex. pills are not the same and are no good!) So I think you're doing fine and will outlast us all. But I'm glad to report that my back is no longer painful. – altho I'll never have a strong spine and can't do much bending, stooping or lifting. I spent over $1000.00 on treatments (no insurance of any kind) But it was worth it to avoid an operation.

title: Slim Brundage letters, 1965-1972
transcription:
Last time I talked to Nancy, she said Suzy's house was going to be auctioned. Said she'd call us about going down to look at it with her. But didn't hear from her. Maybe they found a buyer. I still have Altadena house but am determined to get rid of it in fall. Don't know whether Don can finish the painting so will probably have to hire someone pretty soon. Only kitchen and one bedroom less to do.
Jane says she's having Poetry Meetings at her pad – but she never tells me what's going on, who's there etc. So I'd be glad to hear more details. I've asked her for her phone number and days & hours of Poetry Meetings so I can call sometime and say Hello to everybody. If she forgets to tell me, will you please send me info?
Thanks for curriculum for August. The topics sound interesting. Too bad attendance is off. Summer? 
My birthday is this Sat. (Sept 2) Janet will come over and cook birthday dinner. Not going out of town this year because it's in middle of Labor Day weekend – (no time to travel) but hope to go to San Francisco around Sept. 21st for Book Fair up there this year.
Love from all
Virgine
I stay up until 4 or 5 AM reading in my antique contour rocker – a habit I got into when my back was so bad.
Reading mostly biography – and I meet the most fascinating characters:

title: Slim Brundage letters, 1965-1972
transcription:
Sept 16, 1972
El Grito del Dolores
and
The Day After Don's Birthday
2 AM
Dear Slimbo:
It seems I'm always writing to you on some Mexican fiesta/holiday or other! Have just now put Don to bed SOBER after celebrating his birthday. The big news here is that Don has joined AA (12 days ago). It took a little persuasion but he has a nice guy for his sponsor — and he's take to it like a duck to water. He has to go to a meeting (2 hrs. every evening) which cuts into his TV watching but I'm sure he enjoys his meetings more than he did the poetry meetings in Chicago. Tonight, being his birthday, I went with him, and even cold sober I really enjoyed the speakers. One guy was better than any I ever heard at the College — and last week I heard a hard-boiled dame of 65 (ex-waitress, widow of a truck driver) who has probably the largest vocabulary of racy slang in the world. Wish I'd had the tape recorder with me — but it would have been illegal. They're not all of them that great, but I was lucky the 2 meetings I've been to. However, I'm not going on the wagon myself.

title: Slim Brundage letters, 1965-1972
transcription:
2// Just the day before your letter, I had heard from Jane about Byrd, and I can't tell you how sorry I am. He was a sweet guy — and I used to tell you how he fairly worshipped you. I know you didn't believe it, but it was true. Why do all the nice people die young and we old buzzard hang on to the fence? My darling Joey died when both he and I were 47. It should have been me. At that time, too, I lost (to death) 3 of the finest of my women friends. I have a theory that if people can make it throught their 40s, they have it made. Very few die in their 50s. This is no comfort (there isn't any) but it seems to be a law of life.
Nancy didn't tell me about Byrd — but I know she knew him as a child and it must have added to her sorrow about Suzie. I hope you can console each other. 
We were to have gone (the 3 of us) to the Mitchell's on Labor Day — but that was the day Don chose for his last Big Drunk (starting at 6 PM the day before) He was too drunk to drive us over so at 1 PM I had to call Nancy that we couldn't come. It was about that time that Don called AA and went to his first meeting still drunk. So far he hasn't taken another drink. Please don't

title: Slim Brundage letters, 1965-1972
transcription:
3// mention any of this when you write to us. He will have to tell you himself. You know they're supposed to say "I'm an alcoholic" for the rest of their lives.
This coming Wed. we're driving up to San Francisco. Forgot to tell you the other News: we turned in the Chrysler wagon on a Chrysler 4-door which is 3 yrs. younger and has air-conditioning & other comfortable features. While in S.F. (about 5 days) Don will be going to AA meetings there in the evenings while I attend the Antiquarian Book Fair held by all my book dealer buddies. The rest of the time we'll spend sight-seeing and eating. It will be a nice vacation for both of us.
The College Curriculum sounds good for Sept. You sure got a timely "scoop" on Sept. 2nd (my birthday) with that Israeli program! But what have you got against poor old Ben Franklin? He's one of my heroes — because he was a printer, not because of the ladies. But you must admit, he wasn't a hypocrite about his sex-life. I always liked it that he advised young men to go for older women, especially for the reason that the old dames are so grateful (Also grateful that he didn't say "old bags")
Love from all
Virgine
